observed.title: Compose independent admission gates; held work queues instead of failing fast
observed.statement: An execution admission decision should AND several independent gates (per-entity capacity, global cap, provider-quota cooldown, host resource pressure). When any soft gate is closed, admit() enqueues the work instead of running it into a known failure, and every drain path re-checks the same gates. Cooldown setters must never shorten an active cooldown.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/engine/src/queue.rs` `ConcurrencyTracker::admit` requires `persona_ok && global_ok && quota_ok && resource_ok`; when only quota/resource are closed it logs "Admission held ... enqueuing instead of running" and falls through to the priority queue. `drain_next` / `drain_next_global` re-check `quota_available()` and `resource_available()` before promoting. `set_quota_cooldown` takes the LATER of old/new deadline ("a burst of limit-failures doesn't prematurely lift the pause") — pinned by `test_quota_cooldown_never_shortens` and `test_admit_enqueues_during_cooldown_even_with_capacity`.

observed.title: Warn on the crossing, not the level — latch per rejection streak, reset on admission
observed.statement: A guard that rejects high-frequency calls (rate limiter, breaker) must log its warning once per rejection STREAK via a latch, and reset the latch the moment a request is admitted again — otherwise a hammering caller floods the log with one warning per call, or (if never reset) a later independent streak never warns at all.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/engine/src/rate_limiter.rs` `Bucket.warned` latch with the comment "Signal the crossing, not the level: warn once per rejection streak ... a caller hammering a limit would otherwise flood the log with one warning per request." Regression tests `test_warn_latch_sets_on_first_rejection_and_stays_set` and `test_warn_latch_resets_after_admission_so_next_streak_warns_again` pin both halves. Periodic bucket pruning is piggybacked on every 100th `check()` call while already holding the lock, so bounded memory needs no background task.

observed.title: Both sides of a fingerprint check must call one canonical hash function
observed.statement: When cache reuse depends on a config fingerprint, the write site and the read site must share ONE exported hash helper over the same inputs. If each side hand-rolls a hash over slightly different inputs, the comparison never matches and the cache is a silent permanent no-op — everything cold-starts while looking healthy.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/engine/src/session_pool.rs` `compute_config_hash` doc: "the two sites previously hand-rolled hashes over disjoint inputs (execution_config JSON vs persona fields), so `take` never matched and warm session reuse was a permanent no-op — every run cold-started. Always call this helper from both sides." Test `offer_take_round_trip_with_shared_hash` pins the round trip; `take` also consumes the entry (single-use resume) and invalidates on TTL or hash mismatch.

observed.title: In a windowed global breaker, one success offsets exactly one failure
observed.statement: When a global circuit breaker counts failures across providers in a rolling window, a success must remove at most ONE matching failure entry (1:1 offset), never purge the provider's whole history — a single lucky success would otherwise mask cascading failures and stop the global breaker from ever tripping.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/engine/failover.rs` `record_success`: "Only the most recent failure for this provider is removed (1:1 offset). This prevents a single lucky success from purging the entire failure history, which could mask systemic failures across other providers." Implemented via `rposition` + `remove`. Pinned by `test_single_success_does_not_purge_all_provider_failures` and `test_multiple_successes_gradually_drain_failures`. The same file layers a per-provider breaker (5 consecutive) under a global pause (10 failures / 120s) so a failover chain cannot amplify load on an already-stressed service.

observed.title: Failover chains that pin model ids rot into guaranteed failure
observed.statement: A model-fallback ladder hardcoding provider model ids will eventually hand a healthy run to a retired id — turning failover into a guaranteed 404. Keep the chain on the same canonical current ids the rest of the codebase bakes into configs, and pin it with a regression test asserting retired ids are unreachable.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/engine/failover.rs` `CLAUDE_MODEL_CHAIN` doc: the previous chain pinned `claude-opus-4-20250514` / `claude-sonnet-4-20250514`, "both retired 2026-06-15 and now returning 404 — so a healthy opus persona whose primary hiccuped was actively failed *over into a guaranteed 404*." The fixed chain reuses the canonical ids from `tier_slug_to_model_id`, and `test_failover_chain_never_reaches_retired_ids` asserts both retired ids are absent and a real downgrade candidate exists.

observed.title: Document the degenerate shape of generic machinery, and mark the one re-entry seam
observed.statement: When a generic mechanism (multi-provider failover, plugin dispatch) currently has only one participant, document what it honestly degrades to ("a breaker-gated single-candidate probe") and mark the exact code seam where a second participant re-enters — so callers stop assuming richness that isn't there and future extension is a one-arm change.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/engine/failover.rs` `build_failover_chain` carries an "# Honest shape today (single-provider era)" doc section ("Callers must not assume a rich multi-provider chain") plus an explicit "EXTENSION POINT (cross-provider / BYOM alternates)" comment on the single `match primary { EngineKind::ClaudeCode => vec![] }` arm, noting everything downstream (breaker, per-candidate spawn loop) is already provider-generic.

observed.title: Gate new admissions on host load with hysteresis and asymmetric watermarks; never interrupt running work
observed.statement: A resource governor that pauses work under CPU/memory pressure should (1) only defer NEW admissions, never kill running work; (2) use pause/resume hysteresis (pause when EITHER metric crosses its high watermark, resume only when BOTH fall below lower resume watermarks) so spikes don't flap the gate; (3) set memory's bar higher than CPU's because high RAM use is often healthy cache; and (4) skip the first sample of a delta-based metric, which is bogus.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/engine/resource_governor.rs` — CPU 70/55, MEM 85/70 with a rationale comment ("70%+ used RAM is often normal idle... the OOM kill happens near ~95%"), `if !m.sample_valid { continue; }` for the first CPU delta, and "Running executions are NEVER interrupted — only NEW admissions defer to the per-persona queues." Pinned in `queue.rs` by `test_resource_throttle_queues_then_resumes`.

observed.title: Drain a child process's pipes concurrently with wait(), or chatty output deadlocks it
observed.statement: Awaiting child.wait() before reading stdout/stderr deadlocks any subprocess that emits more than the OS pipe buffer (~64KB): the child blocks on write, wait() never returns, and every chatty run burns its full timeout. Join the wait and both pipe reads concurrently; on timeout, kill the child and salvage the partial buffers.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/engine/src/verification_command.rs` `run_verification` uses `tokio::join!(child.wait(), read stdout, read stderr)` with the comment: "The previous code awaited wait() first and only then read the pipes — a command emitting more than the ~64KB pipe buffer blocked on write, wait() never returned, and every chatty verification ran to its full timeout." On `tokio::time::timeout` expiry it `start_kill()`s the child and still returns the bounded, char-boundary-safe output tail for the downstream fix prompt.

observed.title: Serde casing attributes are wire contracts — pin them with a comment naming the consumers
observed.statement: The field casing an event/IPC payload serializes with is a cross-boundary contract. A well-meaning cleanup that adds (or removes) `rename_all = "camelCase"` silently changes every key on the wire; untyped consumers read `undefined` and misbehave in ways far from the change. Pin the deliberate casing with a comment that names the exact consumer files and describes the failure a change would cause.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/engine/src/process_activity.rs` `ProcessActivityEvent`: "Fields serialize as snake_case ON THE WIRE — deliberately NO rename_all... Re-adding `#[serde(rename_all = \"camelCase\")]` would emit `runId`, so the bridge would read `payload.run_id === undefined` and store every run under the bare 'execution' key — collapsing concurrent/team runs into one and clearing the shared key on the first completion. That breaks FleetActivityStrip + the Monitor's lookup. Keep snake_case." Names both consumer files (`eventRegistry.ts`, `eventBridge.ts`).

observed.title: Dedupe state-crossing alerts with a durable one-row episode, so restarts never re-announce
observed.statement: Breach/recovery alerting should be an enter-once state machine backed by ONE durable row per entity: a crossing INTO breach emits exactly one 'opened' event and writes the episode row; failing runs while open are no-ops; crossing back emits one 'recovered' and closes the row. Because the state lives in a table (not memory), a process restart mid-episode never re-announces an already-open breach. Emission is best-effort and can never break the completion path that triggered it.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/engine/src/sla_breach.rs` — module doc: "`sla_breach_episodes` holds one durable row per persona. A breach emits exactly ONE `sla.breach.opened`... Because the state is a table, a restart mid-episode never re-announces." `evaluate_on_completion` is "cheap (one bounded query) and best-effort: any read/write failure is logged and swallowed so it can never break the execution that triggered it." The pure `decide(episode.is_open, &signal)` state machine lives in the db repo; the recovery event echoes the original open reason and `opened_at` so episode duration is derivable.

observed.title: Register middleware and listeners under a dedup key so hot-reload replaces instead of accumulates
observed.statement: Any module-level registry that closures register into (pipeline middleware, event handlers) must key registrations by a stable string and replace on re-registration — otherwise HMR / remount re-registers a new closure each time and handlers silently run N times. Pair the key with an explicit numeric priority plus an insertion sequence for a stable execution order.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/lib/execution/pipeline.ts` `addMiddleware` — `MiddlewareOptions.key`: "If a middleware with the same key already exists for the stage, it is replaced. This prevents HMR from accumulating duplicate entries when a component re-mounts with a new closure." Entries sort by `(priority, seq)` for deterministic order; consumers like `src/lib/execution/middleware/budgetMiddleware.ts` register as `{ key: 'budget-invalidation', priority: 20 }`.

observed.title: Snapshot the data a post-completion hook needs into the event payload, before state resets
observed.statement: When completion handlers reset shared state and downstream middleware still needs pre-reset facts (recent history, owner id), capture those facts into the completion payload at emit time instead of letting the middleware read the store later — by the time async middleware runs, the store has been reset or repointed at a different entity.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/lib/execution/pipeline.ts` `FrontendCompletePayload.recentExecutions`: "Pre-captured recent executions for the persona, snapshotted before state reset. Avoids the drift middleware reading stale/wrong data from the store." Consumed in `src/lib/execution/middleware/driftMiddleware.ts` ("Use the pre-captured snapshot from the payload (captured before state reset in finishExecution) so we don't read stale or wrong-persona data"); `src/hooks/execution/usePersonaExecution.ts` similarly captures `execPersonaId`/name before `finishExecution`.

observed.title: An async listener attach needs an in-flight flag, or unmount-during-setup leaks or double-frees the subscription
observed.statement: When attaching a subscription is asynchronous (await listen(...)), a subscriber can unmount while setup is still in flight. Teardown must not run while setup is in flight (there is nothing to unlisten yet); instead the setup completion handler must check for zero subscribers and immediately unlisten what it just created. Symmetrically, ad-hoc listeners need a `cancelled` flag checked after the await so a late-resolving attach is torn down instead of stored.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/hooks/realtime/createSingletonListener.ts` — `setupInFlight` flag; `teardownIfEmpty` early-returns while setup is in flight ("the setup completion handler above will clean up when it resolves and finds zero subscribers"), and `ensureListener`'s completion does `if (subscribers.size === 0) { unlisten(); ... }`. The same shape appears ad hoc in `src/hooks/execution/usePersonaExecution.ts` queue/background listeners: `if (!cancelled) { ref.current = unlisten } else { unlisten(); }`.

observed.title: Every terminal event needs exactly one responsible finalizer — navigation must hand off, never orphan
observed.statement: When a focused stream listener owns finalizing a run's terminal event and navigation tears that listener down mid-run, the terminal event can end up handled by NEITHER the focused nor the background listener — busy-state flags then stick until an unrelated watchdog fires. On teardown-while-running, set an explicit 'detached' flag that transfers finalization responsibility to the background listener; clear it when a fresh stream attaches.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/hooks/execution/usePersonaExecution.ts` `focusedStreamDetachedRef` — persona-switch cleanup sets it ("otherwise the event is handled by neither listener and isExecuting sticks for up to 30 min", execution-runner #2); the background EXECUTION_STATUS listener finalizes a detached run's terminal event "regardless of which persona is now selected, so activeExecutionId / isExecuting / the recovery key always clear on terminal"; a fresh execution attach resets the flag.

observed.title: Owner-entity checks are not run correlation — a prior run's late terminal event tears down the live run
observed.statement: Filtering lifecycle events by owning-entity id cannot distinguish two successive runs of the SAME entity: a late or duplicated terminal event from the previous run passes the owner check and tears down the new run's UI state while it keeps running headless. Correlate every lifecycle event against the specific run-instance id, falling through only when no id is present (legacy).
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/hooks/execution/usePersonaExecution.ts` `handleStatusEvent`: "Owner-alignment alone can't distinguish two runs of the same persona, so a late/duplicated terminal event for a PRIOR run could tear down the live run's UI (clear activeExecutionId, stop output, drop the recovery key) while it keeps running headless (bug-hunt 2026-06-07 execution #5)." Guard: `if (eventExecId && focusedExecId && eventExecId !== focusedExecId) return;`.

observed.title: Insert-first idempotency: the pre-check is only an optimization; the partial unique index is the guarantee
observed.statement: For idempotency-keyed creates, a SELECT-then-INSERT pre-check is a TOCTOU race (double-delivered webhooks, timeout retries). Do the INSERT with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING against a partial unique index on the key (the conflict target must repeat the index's WHERE clause), and on rows_changed == 0 re-select and return the winner's row so retries are transparently idempotent. NULL keys stay outside the partial index and always insert.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/db/src/repos/execution/executions.rs` `create_with_idempotency` — `ON CONFLICT(idempotency_key) WHERE idempotency_key IS NOT NULL DO NOTHING` with the comment: "Insert-first with conflict handling so a concurrent same-key insert (a lost TOCTOU race against the pre-check above — e.g. a double-delivered webhook or a timeout-retry) dedups instead of hard-erroring... The conflict target repeats that partial index's WHERE clause so SQLite selects it." `rows_changed == 0` → re-select by key and return existing.

observed.title: Cancellation is a terminal sink: a result landing after Stop must never resurrect success
observed.statement: Status finalization needs asymmetric compare-and-swap rules: only the cancel branch may write over an existing 'cancelled' row (to enrich a bare safety-net cancel with metrics); every other terminal status may only advance a still-'running' row. Without the split, a completion landing in the window just after the user clicks Stop clobbers the freshly-written cancel back to 'completed' — lost-cancel plus success theater.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/db/src/repos/execution/executions.rs` `update_status_if_not_final`: `WHERE id = ? AND status IN ('running','cancelled')` for the cancelled branch vs `WHERE ... AND status = 'running'` for everything else, with the comment "Cancellation is a terminal sink: a completion/failure must NEVER overwrite a user cancel... a result landing in the window just after the user clicks Stop clobbers the freshly-written 'cancelled' row back to 'completed' (lost-cancel + success theater)."

observed.title: A re-claimed job must re-stamp its start timestamp, or the zombie sweep kills healthy retries
observed.statement: If a watchdog judges liveness by started_at, then started_at must mean 'when the CURRENT attempt began'. Preserving the first attempt's timestamp across a running→queued→running re-claim (COALESCE(started_at, now)) makes a freshly re-claimed healthy run look like an hours-old zombie, and the sweep drops its real result. Stamp started_at unconditionally on every claim.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/db/src/repos/execution/executions.rs` `claim_for_instance`: "started_at is stamped UNCONDITIONALLY: a claim IS the start of a run attempt. Previously `COALESCE(started_at, ?4)` preserved the first attempt's timestamp across a re-claim (quota cooldown / crash-recovery re-queue), so `sweep_zombie_executions` — which reads started_at as 'when the CURRENT attempt began' — would flag a freshly re-claimed, healthy run as a >30-min zombie and drop its real result." The claim itself is CAS with a TTL-in-WHERE that doubles as the stale-claim sweep (expired claims are simply re-claimable, no reaper task), and the comment pins all writers to RFC3339 so lexicographic `<` stays chronological.

observed.title: A breaker's streak means failures since the last success, excluding environmental causes
observed.statement: Two ways a 'consecutive failures' breaker silently degrades: (1) counting the last N failed rows regardless of interleaved successes means any entity with N lifetime failures permanently reads as 'N consecutive'; (2) counting environment-caused failures (rate/usage/session limits, app-restart kills) trips the breaker on conditions that say nothing about the entity itself. Compute the streak as failures newer than the last success, with the environmental class explicitly excluded.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/db/src/repos/execution/executions.rs` `count_consecutive_real_failures`: "TRUE consecutive-failure streak for the circuit breaker: failures SINCE the persona's last completed execution (`get_recent_failures(...).len()` counted the last N failed rows regardless, so any persona with >= N lifetime failures permanently read as 'N consecutive'), EXCLUDING environmental failures... One quota storm must not trip the breaker." SQL: `created_at > COALESCE((SELECT MAX(created_at) ... status='completed'), '1970-01-01')` plus NOT-LIKE exclusions.

observed.title: Every failure class you exempt from a breaker needs its own dedicated bound
observed.statement: Exempting a failure class (e.g. provider-environmental errors) from the entity circuit breaker removes the only thing bounding retries of that class: each new run starts a fresh retry chain and the breaker never trips. Add a complementary windowed counter over exactly the exempted class, and past a documented cap, convert the auto-retry into a surfaced manual issue. Bound retry COUNT, not wait time, so one legitimate long wait still schedules.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/db/src/repos/execution/executions.rs` `count_environmental_failures_in_window`: "These are exactly the failures the persona circuit breaker EXCLUDES — so during a sustained provider incident nothing else bounds the *cross-chain* retry storm... The healing orchestrator reads this count and, past a documented cap, folds the auto-retry into a manual issue instead of piling on another scheduled retry. The window bounds RETRY COUNT, not wait time — a single legitimate usage-window wait (hours) still schedules normally." The LIKE shapes deliberately mirror the breaker's exclusion list so the two guards partition the same taxonomy.

observed.title: Zero can mean unknown: exclude cost-unknown candidates from value rankings instead of treating 0 as free
observed.statement: A provider whose per-call cost is hardcoded 0.0 (because it is UNKNOWN, e.g. local models) scores as a perfect-efficiency free model in any cost-weighted value ranking and always wins. Model 'cost unknown' as an explicit flag and exclude flagged candidates from best-value verdicts entirely — returning 'unknown' when every candidate is flagged — rather than letting a sentinel zero masquerade as free.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/engine/src/test_runner.rs` — `compute_value_score` NOTE ("a caller must not pass a cost of 0.0 for a *cost-unknown* model expecting a meaningful value"), `provider_cost_is_known` ("Ollama's cost is hardcoded to 0.0 in the runner, so a zero there means 'unknown', not 'free'"), and `best_value_model` filtering `cost_unknown` rankings. Tests under "Direction 2: best-value must not be awarded on hardcoded-zero cost" pin the exclusion.

observed.title: Flag reconstructed telemetry as synthetic and badge it, never present estimates as measurements
observed.statement: When a trace/timeline is reconstructed from coarse endpoints instead of captured live, mark the reconstructed object with an explicit `isSynthetic` flag and have every renderer show an 'Estimated' badge — millisecond-precision guesses presented as fact mislead operators. Note that live vs synthetic are independent axes: a historical execution can have a real captured trace (neither), and a synthetic trace is never the live one.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/agents/sub_executions/trace/SyntheticTrace.ts` `SyntheticPipelineTrace.isSynthetic` ("lets a renderer distinguish this from a real captured trace... 'Estimated' badge instead of presenting ms-precision guesses as fact") with a dedicated regression test in `SyntheticTrace.test.ts`; consumed by `replay/PipelineWaterfall.tsx` (comment: an execution can be "neither ... nor both") and `replay/CostAccrualOverlay.tsx` which also labels its cost split as a "proportional reconstruction ... never a" measured value.

observed.title: Audit why an automation cascade did NOT continue, one structured row per non-continuation
observed.statement: Every non-continuation path in a chained-automation evaluator (suppressed handoff, cycle skip, depth ceiling, unmet predicate, quarantine, cost ceiling, healing abandonment) should write a structured stop-reason row keyed by the distributed trace id — machine reason token + human detail + depth — so an operator can answer 'why did this chain stop?'. Writes are best-effort: a lost audit row must never fail the cascade. Whole-cascade halts carry NULL trigger references since they aren't tied to one link.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/db/src/repos/execution/chain_stop_reasons.rs` — module doc: "Before this table, every non-continuation was silent... Each is now recorded as a row keyed by `chain_trace_id`." Reason vocabulary is a closed token set (`crate::chain::stop_reason`), resolved to labels via frontend token maps; `record` is called best-effort from the cascade evaluator ("a failed write never fails the cascade"); healing-abandonment tokens round-trip through the same path (test `healing_stop_reason_tokens_round_trip`).

observed.title: Run every fallible lookup BEFORE taking the permanent claim, and never collapse a fallible read into its empty default
observed.statement: In a claim-then-work loop, any fallible read whose result decides what the work is must run before the atomic claim: if it runs after, a transient error (DB busy/lock) gets locked in by the already-stamped claim and the work is permanently stranded. On read error, skip WITHOUT claiming so the next tick retries. The enabling bug is often `.ok()...unwrap_or_default()`, which collapses 'transient error' and 'legitimately empty' into the same value — return a real Result instead.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/engine/incident_continuation.rs` — `failed_assignment_steps` returns "a real `Result` (NOT a swallowed empty `Vec`)... The old inline `.ok() … .unwrap_or_default()` collapsed both into an empty vec, which — after the continuation claim was already stamped — permanently mis-classified a transient error as 'already resumed' and stranded the assignment." The loop comment: "Run that lookup BEFORE taking the permanent claim... On Err we skip WITHOUT claiming, so `continued_at` stays NULL and the next tick retries." The claim itself is `UPDATE ... SET continued_at = now WHERE id = ? AND continued_at IS NULL` (at-most-once regardless of overlap or restart).

observed.title: Refuse to re-run agent work without the original task context
observed.statement: An automated continuation/retry of agent work must abort when the original input is missing or unparseable, rather than starting a contextless re-run. NULL and unparseable inputs silently collapsing to None produce a run that fabricates work off a hallucinated reconstruction — potentially taking real, irreversible actions — while logging a 'successful continuation'. Abort, leave the item claimed-but-not-continued, and surface it for a human.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/engine/incident_continuation.rs` — "Previously NULL and unparseable input_data both silently collapsed to None, starting a contextless re-run that fabricates work (or runs against empty input) while logging a 'successful continuation' — and could take real, irreversible actions off a hallucinated reconstruction. Abort instead, leaving the incident claimed-but-not-continued for human attention." The same function also re-checks `is_simulation` at the continuation site ("a dry-run must never spawn a real follow-up") even though the promote site already guards it.

observed.title: An automated rollback must verify the TARGET is genuinely healthier, with symmetric minimum-sample floors
observed.statement: Rolling back automatically on 'current error rate > 2x previous' is not enough. Apply the minimum-execution floor to BOTH sides — a target whose 0% error rate is one lucky run is not a track record — and require the target's rate to be strictly lower than the current AND under an absolute ceiling; otherwise a 90%-error version gets confidently 'rolled back' onto an 80%-error version. Use execution-weighted (not per-day) error rates, and put a noise floor under the trigger threshold.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/engine/auto_rollback.rs` — `MIN_EXECUTIONS_FOR_COMPARISON` applied "symmetrically to the current version AND the rollback target: without it we could roll onto a version whose 0% error rate is a single lucky run"; the target gate `previous_error_rate >= current_error_rate || previous_error_rate > ROLLBACK_TARGET_MAX_ERROR_RATE (0.5)` with the comment about landing on a still-broken version "while emitting a confident auto_rollback event"; `threshold = (previous * 2.0).max(0.1)` to avoid rolling back on 0→0.01 noise; `compute_weighted_error_rate` weights by execution count.

observed.title: Identify the active version by an explicit tag, never by max(version_number)
observed.statement: After a rollback, the demoted version still carries the highest version number. Selecting 'current' by sorting on version number re-selects the demoted version on every evaluation tick — an infinite rollback loop. Tag the active version explicitly (e.g. tag='production'), select by tag, and perform demote-all-then-promote inside one transaction so two rows can never both be tagged active.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/engine/auto_rollback.rs` — "Use the version tagged 'production' as current rather than the highest version_number. After a rollback the demoted version still has a higher number but is tagged 'experimental', so sorting by number alone would re-select the demoted version every tick, causing an infinite loop." `perform_rollback` demotes ALL production rows and promotes the target within one SQLite transaction ("avoids the race where get_production_version() returns None (or a stale row) outside the transaction... leaving two versions tagged 'production'"), and restores both prompt fields atomically — absent fields explicitly NULLed to prevent 'Frankenstein' mixed-version state.

observed.title: Off-thread compute behind a same-API fallback, with crash recovery that rejects all pending and resets the singleton
observed.statement: Wrap expensive pure computation (diffing, parsing) in a lazily-created Web Worker client that (1) falls back to the identical synchronous implementation when Worker is unavailable or construction throws, so callers have one API; (2) correlates requests by monotonic id with per-request cancel; (3) on worker error rejects EVERY pending promise and terminates + resets the singleton to undefined so the next call transparently re-creates it; and (4) memoizes results by a cheap content hash so repeat comparisons skip the worker entirely.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/agents/sub_executions/libs/comparisonDiffWorkerClient.ts` — tri-state `worker: Worker | null | undefined` (undefined = untried, null = unavailable → inline `diffLines`/`jsonDiff` fallback), `pendingLine`/`pendingJson` maps keyed by request id, `worker.onerror` rejecting all pending then `terminate(); worker = undefined`, and FNV-hash `diffCacheKey` caches. The worker streams `line-chunk` messages so large diffs paint incrementally.

observed.title: A reusable stream consumer must let the caller opt out of its internal buffer
observed.statement: When a generic streaming hook keeps its own bounded line buffer and a consumer pipes the same lines into an external store, the same stream is buffered twice with divergent trim points. Expose an explicit opt-out (bufferLines: false) so exactly one owner holds the data, and read the flag through a ref so the listener closure sees updates without destabilizing the start callback's identity.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/hooks/execution/useCorrelatedCliStream.ts` `bufferLines` option; consumed by `src/hooks/execution/usePersonaExecution.ts` with the comment "The execution store (executionSlice) is the single source of truth for terminal output. Disable the hook's own 5000-line buffer to prevent duplicate memory usage and divergent trim points." Callback refs (`onFailedRef` etc.) keep `start` referentially stable — "any inline arrow function causes `start` to be recreated every render, which can trigger infinite update loops."

observed.title: Mirror a cross-language status enum from generated bindings and derive its terminal/active sets in one place
observed.statement: When a state machine's enum lives in the backend and the frontend needs it, re-export the codegen'd binding type rather than re-declaring the union, add frontend-only extensions (an 'unknown' corruption fallback) at that single seam, and derive the TERMINAL/ACTIVE sets plus the valid-transition map in the same module — so a new variant has exactly one frontend place to update, with a backend compile-time test enforcing its side of the parity.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/lib/execution/executionState.ts` — re-exports ts-rs-generated `ExecutionState` from `@/lib/bindings`, adds `'unknown'` ("Unrecognised values map to 'unknown' (not 'failed') so data corruption is visible in the UI instead of masquerading as a real failure"), declares `TERMINAL_STATES`/`ACTIVE_STATES` with "These MUST match the Rust TERMINAL / ACTIVE slices in engine/types.rs. A Rust compile-time test enforces the Rust side", plus `VALID_TRANSITIONS` and the legacy `'pending'→'queued'` alias handled at the single parse seam.

observed.title: Persist monotonic-clock state across restarts via elapsed-to-wall-clock conversion under a short TTL
observed.statement: Instant-based transient state (an open circuit's opened_at) can survive restarts: persist it by converting elapsed time to an RFC3339 wall-clock timestamp, and on restore reconstruct the approximate Instant with now - elapsed (checked_sub, clamped to now). Restore only rows younger than a short TTL and purge the rest — stale transient state is worse than starting fresh — and treat every restore/persist error as best-effort (worst case: start clean).
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/engine/failover.rs` `ProviderCircuitBreaker::with_persistence` — `PERSIST_TTL_MINUTES = 15` ("States older than this are ignored on restore and periodically purged"); restore parses the persisted ISO time, computes elapsed, and does `Instant::now().checked_sub(elapsed).unwrap_or_else(Instant::now)`; `persist_all` does the inverse (`Utc::now() - opened.elapsed()`); restore failure logs and starts fresh ("ignore errors — worst case we start fresh").

observed.title: Track each data family's fetch lifecycle with a stale state distinct from failed
observed.statement: When a screen composes several independently fetched data families, give each family its own status ('idle'|'loading'|'loaded'|'failed'|'stale') where a failed RELOAD of previously loaded data goes 'stale' (keep showing it, flag it) instead of 'failed' (nothing to show). A retry action sweeps every failed/stale family, replaying remembered inputs for parameterized loads.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/lib/sceneStore.ts` — `FamilyStatus` doc comment ('stale = loaded once but a newer load failed, so the shown data is real but no longer guaranteed current'), `failStatus(prev)` returning `stale` for loaded/stale and `failed` otherwise, and `retryFailed()` which replays `lastSentryInputs`/`lastLlmSpendInputs` for the two parameterized families. The page renders 'an honest data-health banner (never a silent partial truth)' from these statuses (`DataHealthBar`). Six families (meta/scans/sentry/goals/runners/llmSpend) each carry their own status so one failure never hides five healthy families.

observed.title: A failed fetch renders as unknown, never as a fake absent
observed.statement: Derivation functions that turn fetched data into status cells must accept a per-family 'hard-failed' flag and emit a distinct 'unknown' status for it — because 'never scanned', 'no KPIs', and 'we could not load the data' are three different truths, and collapsing the last into either of the others makes the UI lie. Aggregation rollups must also rank unknown worse than healthy so a failed family can never read as green.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/lib/deriveScene.ts` `FamilyHealth` ('drives the unknown cell state so a failed fetch never renders as a fake "never scanned" / "absent"'); `dimRegistry.ts` kpi/ideas/goals derives each short-circuit to `status: 'unknown'` on `kpiUnknown`/`scansUnknown`/`goalsUnknown`; `dimCategories.ts` `rollupStatus` places `unknown` above partial/absent/solid ('a failed data family must not read as healthy') and `STATUS_RANK` sorts it third-worst. Same doctrine in `liveState.ts`: projects without a supported monitoring credential are simply ABSENT from the map ('no fake green, no fake red' — readiness-only colour).

observed.title: Collapse scattered localStorage keys into one versioned document with sync reads over async hydration
observed.statement: Migrate N machine-local localStorage keys into ONE versioned JSON document in the durable settings store: hydrate once at mount (idempotent, promise-memoized, never rejects), keep the module API synchronous over the in-memory doc so no caller signature changes, write through with a debounced coalescing flush, do a one-time legacy import when the DB doc is absent, and degrade to a single localStorage key when IPC is unavailable. The storage KEY stays stable across doc versions — the version FIELD is what moves.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/lib/layoutStore.ts` — `LAYOUT_KEY = 'mastermind.layout.v1'` with 'the key is stable across doc versions; the version FIELD is what moves'; `hydrateLayout()` returns the same in-flight promise on concurrent calls and 'never rejects — IPC failure degrades to the localStorage path'; sync `loadPositions()/saveGroups()` API over the hydrated doc; `WRITE_DEBOUNCE_MS = 500` coalescing flush; one-time `readLegacyLocal()` import persisted immediately so 'thereafter the DB is the source of truth and the legacy keys are left as a stale backup'; `parseLayout` coerces every field and falls back to empty on malformed input. Companion invariant: opaque versioned sub-payloads are guarded at BOTH doors — `parsePanels` drops unsupported `specVersion` on read ('tolerate-and-drop — never retained as a poison value a renderer would have to defend against') and `saveAthenaPanel` refuses them on write.

observed.title: Make a two-writer shared document safe with one mutable copy plus per-object author provenance
observed.statement: When an AI agent and the user edit the same board concurrently: (1) keep ONE mutable in-memory copy that views subscribe to via useSyncExternalStore instead of snapshotting into useState — so an out-of-band write renders immediately and the next user commit builds on the post-write array, not a stale one; (2) stamp every object with an author field so the agent's objects can be visually distinguished and reverted WITHOUT touching the user's. Migration attribution must default to the human: anything not literally the agent's marker is the user's, because 'attribution can only ever ADD provenance, never take an object away from its owner'.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/lib/layoutStore.ts` 'TWO WRITERS' header comment; `coerceAuthor` (`value === 'athena' ? 'athena' : 'user'`); `countAthenaObjects`/`revertAthenaObjects` filtering by `author`; snapshot getters returning the SAME container until a write invalidates (`cache` invalidated in `emit()` — the useSyncExternalStore contract). `CanvasShell.tsx` confirms the consumer side: 'Canvas objects live in the layout store, not in local state: Athena writes to the same board out of band, and a useState snapshot would neither show her work nor survive the next user commit.' Scope discipline: `countAthenaObjects` deliberately excludes composed panels — 'Two scopes, two controls' — so a canvas-wide revert can't silently destroy per-project surfaces.

observed.title: Content-dedupe a debounced publisher by stamping timestamps at write time, not build time
observed.statement: A snapshot publisher that debounces and skips unchanged bodies must stamp its publishedAt/updatedAt timestamp when the write actually happens — a timestamp inside the compared body would make every snapshot look different and defeat the dedupe entirely. On write failure, clear the dedupe memo so the next derive retries instead of believing the failed body was published.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/lib/scenePublish.ts` — `writeNow` comment: '`publishedAt` is stamped HERE, not in the payload builder: a timestamp inside the compared body would make every snapshot look different and defeat the dedupe entirely'; `publishCanvasScene` compares `JSON.stringify(payload)` against `lastBody` and schedules nothing on match ('the steady state costs zero IPC'); the catch path sets `lastBody = null` ('forget the memo so the next derive republishes'). The publisher is triggered on every data-family arrival/fleet tick/drag commit, so both guards are load-bearing.

observed.title: When a view's derived model cannot be reproduced server-side, publish the derivation itself
observed.statement: If a rich client derives state that the backend cannot re-derive (client-only closures over multiple fetch families, including which family FAILED to load in the client), don't try to rebuild it server-side — have the client publish its derived snapshot to a versioned settings key and make every other consumer read that. Document the contract on the consuming (Rust) type; field names match exactly; unknown fields ignored; and never publish demo/fixture scenes — publishing nothing is the honest answer when no real data exists.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/lib/scenePublish.ts` header: 'Nothing in SQLite can reproduce that, and a Rust re-derive could never report which family failed to load in the client. So the canvas publishes what it derived into `mastermind.scene.v1` and every companion surface reads it.' Contract 'documented on `canvas::CanvasScene` in `src-tauri/src/companion/canvas.rs`; the field names below match it exactly (camelCase, every field optional except slug, unknown fields ignored)'. Rule 1: 'Never publish the demo scene… a published demo scene would let Athena describe six projects that are not there.' The same fixture-honesty shows in `deriveScene.ts`: demo islands carry no runner tasks because 'a fixture task would be a lie the Run Desk could not corroborate'.

observed.title: Drive a mounted view from outside by queueing typed requests it answers with honest envelopes
observed.statement: To control a complex view (canvas, map, editor) from external callers — test harnesses, AI agents, deep links — lift the REQUEST, not the state: an external module-level queue of typed actions the view subscribes to and answers using the same callbacks its human affordances use. Every dispatch resolves (never rejects) with a result envelope carrying honest failure reasons and post-action readouts; a pickup timeout fails 'view_closed' when nothing is mounted, and callers that route first (set navigation state, then dispatch) get the timeout window as their carry-across-mount grace period.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/lib/canvasActionStore.ts` — typed `CanvasActionRequest` grammar; `CanvasActionResult` with reasons `unknown_slug|band_too_far|demo_scene|canvas_closed|bad_request` plus `clamped` ('honest acks… rather than silent best-effort, because the v2 consumer narrates from these payloads'); `PICKUP_TIMEOUT_MS = 2000` ('long enough to survive a route-in render; short enough that a caller on the wrong screen learns so promptly'); `takeCanvasActions()` transfers settle ownership to the shell. `focusStore.ts` is the pattern's origin ('lift the REQUEST, not the camera' — off-screen islands are not in the DOM, so no action may be a DOM lookup) with a monotonic `seq` so re-focusing the SAME target reads as a new request. `useCanvasControlBridge.ts` shows the route-then-dispatch consumer: sets sidebar/tab state, then dispatches, relying on the pickup window to carry the action across the mount. `useCanvasCamera.animateTo` returns a settle promise 'what makes programmatic drives deterministic: dispatch → await → read back'.

observed.title: Replace JSON.stringify cache-hit tests with exhaustive field comparators that short-circuit
observed.statement: A per-item render cache over pure-rebuild derived objects cannot compare by identity — but comparing by JSON.stringify allocates a multi-kilobyte string per item, never bails early, and runs once per animation frame during hydration. Write a hand-rolled comparator that walks the same fields, short-circuits on first mismatch, and allocates nothing. Accept and DOCUMENT the one maintenance cost: a new field must be added to the comparator or changes in it paint stale.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/lib/islandEquality.ts` — header quantifies the anti-pattern ('allocates a multi-kilobyte string per island… the page re-enters that loop once per animation frame while the hydration waves drain… the same N strings built dozens of times over') and the cost ('a NEW field on Island or DimNode must be added here too, or… the canvas will paint stale. That is the one maintenance cost of not using a serializer'). `sameIslandContent` deliberately covers page-decorated fields too, 'so it is a complete answer on its own rather than one half of a comparison whose other half lives at the call site.' Consumers pair it with stable empty fallbacks (`MastermindPage.tsx` `EMPTY_FLEET`/`EMPTY_NAMES`/`EMPTY_RUNNERS`: 'a fresh [] per island would defeat the identity cache').

observed.title: Render-free gesture navigation: drive the transform imperatively, commit state on release
observed.statement: For pan/zoom over a large scene, do not route every pointer frame through React state. Pan writes the world transform imperatively via a ref (zero re-renders), commits state exactly once on release, plus periodic mid-gesture commits every N world units so viewport culling follows the camera. Wheel zoom coalesces bursts into ≤1 state commit per animation frame (multiply accumulated factors, keep the latest pivot, flush in rAF). Guard the imperative path against unrelated re-renders: a layout effect re-asserts the live transform so React reconciliation can't snap the view back to the stale committed camera.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/lib/useCanvasCamera.ts` — 'Render-free navigation (round 14)' header; `PAN_COMMIT_WORLD = 350` ('long pans no longer drag across empty sea until release'); `zoomAccum` + `flushZoom` rAF coalescing; the `useLayoutEffect` re-assert ('If a re-render from some OTHER state (fleet poll, hover) lands mid-pan, React reconciles the <g> transform back to the (stale) committed cam. Re-assert the live one so the pan never visibly snaps back'); `camRef` kept exact per tween frame so 'gesture math and the action layer's post-travel readbacks must not lag the tween by a render'; graceful fallback to state commits when no `worldRef` (unit tests). `CanvasShell.tsx` documents the outcome: 'a pan does zero island re-renders and a wheel zoom commits at most once per animation frame' at 50–100 projects / 60fps.

observed.title: Animation settle promises must resolve on cancel too
observed.statement: A programmatic tween that returns a promise must resolve it on completion AND on cancellation (user input interrupting the travel) — an awaiting caller must never hang; it simply observes wherever the camera/animation ended up. Store the resolver in a ref, and have every interrupt path (new tween, wheel, drag, unmount) call it.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/lib/useCanvasCamera.ts` — `animDone` ref: 'Settle notifier for the in-flight tween — resolved on completion AND on cancel (a user wheel/drag interrupting a programmatic travel must not leave an awaiting caller hanging; it observes wherever the camera ended up)'; `cancelTween` invoked from `onWheel`, `onPointerDown`, a new `animateTo`, and the unmount effect. This is what makes the canvas action grammar's dispatch→await→readback deterministic even when a human interrupts an agent's camera travel.

observed.title: One-shot deterministic layout: bounded force pass, no clock or RNG, hashed tie-breaks, pinned anchors
observed.statement: Auto-layout ('tidy') runs a BOUNDED force-directed pass once and snaps to the result — no continuous simulation. Determinism is a hard invariant: no Date, no Math.random anywhere; inputs are sorted; the only tie-break for coincident points is a stable string hash — so identical input always yields identical output (testable, reproducible, diffable). User-pinned nodes are anchors: they exert forces but never move, and when overlap resolution meets two pinned nodes it leaves them alone — the user's explicit layout wins. Overlap resolution is itself a bounded pass (cap on iterations, whole shove onto the free end when one node is pinned).
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/lib/tidyLayout.ts` — header ('NO continuous simulation (repo animation-austerity rule)… Determinism: no Date / Math.random anywhere. Island order is slug-sorted, the only tie-break for coincident points is hash01(slug)'); `MAX_ITERS = 120`, `MAX_OVERLAP_PASSES = 80`; `resolveOverlaps` with 'both fixed — user's explicit layout wins' and `shareA = pinB ? 1 : pinA ? 0 : 0.5`; dead-centre collisions pick 'a stable hashed axis dir'. `hex.ts` `hash01`/`spiralPlace` supply the deterministic base placement; `persistence.test.ts` pins the invariants ('spiralPlace is deterministic per (index, slug)'). `CanvasShell.tsx` pairs the one-shot with single-level undo (`undoSnap` of exact pre-tidy positions).

observed.title: A registry entry per dimension keeps N render surfaces in lockstep and makes adding one a single edit
observed.statement: When many surfaces (scene derivation, menus, glyphs, cell renderers, action routing) all need per-dimension knowledge, centralize label/icon/derive()/action-kind/payload-kind in ONE registry keyed by a const tuple. Deriving the key union from the tuple (not from entry value types) keeps the key space free of circular type references, and `Record<Key, Entry>` makes the compiler flag a key without an entry and vice-versa. Document the 'adding a dimension' recipe at the bottom of the registry file, including the one render-side change that can't be automated.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/lib/dimRegistry.ts` — `DIM_ORDER` const tuple + `type DimKey = typeof DIM_ORDER[number]` ('derived from this tuple (NOT from the registry value types) so the key space stays decoupled… and free of circular type references'); `DIM_REGISTRY: Record<DimKey, DimRegistryEntry>` ('the Record type keeps them in lockstep — the compiler flags a key without an entry and vice-versa'); `addingADimension` footer note listing the single lattice-slot render change. Consumers named in the header: 'deriveScene, dimMeta, dimActions, DimGlyph and both cell renderers all read this registry.' Entries also carry `viewOnly` for dimensions inert BY DESIGN vs by omission ('the cells say so in their tooltip instead of leaving the user clicking a dead square').

observed.title: Every zoom level of an aggregate must reduce from one module so the bands cannot disagree
observed.statement: When a view renders the same underlying data at multiple detail levels (far count, mid breakdown, near full detail), all levels must reduce from ONE pure module — 'a mid breakdown that did not add up to the far count would make one of the two bands a liar, and the operator zooms between them.' Corollaries: filter dead items in the shared module (not at call sites) so no band counts finished work; KEEP unrecognized states rather than dropping them ('an unrecognised state is still a running thing'); and render empty lanes as empty lanes, never omit them — 'a missing lane and a zero-count lane look identical once they are gone.'
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/lib/farProcesses.ts` — header couples the far and mid bands to one reducer; `DEAD_STATES` filter lives in the module 'rather than relying on the caller — "3 running" must never be counting something that finished'; unknown fleet states 'are kept rather than dropped… silently omitting it would make the number lie'; `processLanes` returns 'always all three and always in the same order' with the empty-lane rationale; `isLiveSession` exported so per-session pip surfaces 'must show exactly the set this module counts, or the pips would not sum to the numbers'; `runnerProgress` excludes queued tasks (averaging their 0% 'would read as "this work has stalled" rather than "not started"'). Same shape in `dimCategories.ts`: far/mid category cells reduce from `rollupStatus` with a documented pessimistic-about-problems / strict-about-green rule.

observed.title: Derive graph decorations in one useMemo pass instead of N setState effects
observed.statement: When node/edge arrays are enriched by several independent concerns (base derivation, execution status, optimizer highlights, active-edge state, dry-run decorations), do NOT give each concern its own useEffect calling setNodes/setEdges — replace them with one useMemo that computes the final enriched arrays in a single pass over prebuilt O(1) lookup maps. Eliminates effect-ordering races, redundant renders, and repeated .find() scans.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/teams/sub_canvas/libs/useDerivedCanvasState.ts` — doc comment: 'Replaces 5 individual useEffect hooks that each called setNodes/setEdges… with one useMemo that computes the final enriched arrays in a single pass.' Inside: `personaMap`/`statusMap` Maps built once ('for O(1) access instead of repeated .find()'), edge counts pre-aggregated, ghost edges filtered against real connections, and cycle nodes merged from graph topology + backend confirmation. The reducer companion (`canvasActions.ts` `RESET_ON_TEAM_SWITCH`) resets only run-scoped state on team switch, keeping the derivation inputs clean.

observed.title: Nesting sibling setState calls inside another updater double-applies under StrictMode
observed.statement: React requires setState updaters to be pure. Nesting setNodeData/setCompletedEdges/setActiveEdge calls inside setStepIndex's updater means StrictMode's double-invocation applies the side-effect writes twice per step, and batching changes can reorder them. Compute the step transition OUTSIDE the updaters (read the current value, derive the next step, then issue each setState with its own pure updater).
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/teams/sub_canvas/libs/useDebugger.ts` `executeStep` comment: 'Step transition computed OUTSIDE the updaters: React requires setState updaters to be pure, and the previous version nested setNodeData / setCompletedEdges / setActiveEdge calls inside setStepIndex's updater — under StrictMode's double-invocation the edge/inspection writes applied twice per step, and batching changes could reorder them.' The fixed version derives `nextIdx`/`nodeId` from captured state, then issues independent pure updaters. Also note the paired `pausedRef` mirror of `paused` so the auto-step timeout reads the live value.

observed.title: Multi-step create flows: roll back the parent on member failure, isolate per-edge inserts, count only what persisted
observed.statement: A blueprint-apply flow (create team → add members → create connections → seed extras) needs three distinct failure disciplines: (1) member creation failure rolls back the parent (best-effort delete) so no orphaned half-team survives; (2) per-edge inserts are individually try/caught because an LLM blueprint routinely contains edges the backend legitimately rejects (duplicates, self-loops, cycle-forming) — one bad edge must not abort the whole build, and the reported count reflects rows that actually persisted; (3) optional enrichment (memory seeding) is fully best-effort and capped. Also null-check store actions that swallow backend errors — a null return later throws an unrelated TypeError and surfaces a generic message.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/teams/sub_teamWorkspace/useAutoTeam.ts` `apply()` — member loop throws on null `addTeamMember` result with rollback (`try { await deleteTeam(team.id) } catch …`); connection loop comment: 'Previously any one of those threw straight to the outer catch, surfaced a generic "Failed to create team", and left the already-valid team + members orphaned. Isolate each insert and count only the connections that actually persisted… (and one bad edge can't abort the whole build)'; seeding wrapped in nested silentCatch with a `seeded >= 10` cap; the addTeamMember nullcheck comment names the exact failure cascade it prevents.

observed.title: Phase-state read from the render snapshot cannot guard double-submit — flip a ref synchronously
observed.statement: Two Enter keydowns (or Enter + click) dispatched in the same tick both observe the pre-submit phase state and each run the full multi-step create flow, orphaning the first result. State-based guards ('if phase !== previewing return') are useless here because state updates after re-render. Guard re-entry with a ref that flips synchronously before any await, and release it in finally.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/teams/sub_teamWorkspace/useAutoTeam.ts` — `applyingRef` comment: 'phase is read from the render snapshot, so two Enter keydowns (or Enter + click) dispatched in the same tick both observe previewing and would otherwise both run a full team-creation flow, orphaning the first team. A ref flips synchronously, before any re-render.' `apply()` opens with `if (applyingRef.current) return; applyingRef.current = true;` and clears it in `finally`. Paired with `cancelledRef` checks after every await for stale-completion abandonment.

observed.title: Never write back a record hydrated from a lean list projection — re-read the full record right before the merge-write
observed.statement: List endpoints often return lean projections with heavy fields blanked. Writing an edited record from a list row silently wipes those fields. The discipline: hydrate the full record per detail call for display, AND re-read it again IMMEDIATELY before any write ('the hydration map can be minutes old; another surface may have edited since'), merging the change into the fresh blob. When moving an owned resource between records, remove it from the old owner FIRST so a failed second write can never leave two live owners. Guard concurrent hydrations with a load sequence number so a stale response can't overwrite a newer one.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/teams/sub_teamWorkspace/teamStudio/slackBridge/useTeamSlackBridge.ts` — header: '`list_personas` is a LEAN projection: it returns `notification_channels` BLANK. Writing a bridge from a roster row would therefore persist a channel array built from nothing and wipe every real notification channel on that persona.' `freshBlob()` re-reads via `get_persona_detail` before every merge; `save()` move path: 'drop it from the old one first, so a failed second write can never leave two live bridges for one team'; `loadSeq` ref guards `hydrate()` races (`if (seq !== loadSeq.current) return`). A `legacyBlob` flag surfaces unparseable blobs instead of overwriting them.

observed.title: Presence from an append-only feed: time-bound the working state, leave the waiting state unbounded
observed.statement: Deriving liveness ('working' / 'waiting') from a paged event feed must acknowledge that the terminal row clearing a state may simply never arrive (crash, cancel, machine sleep). So 'working' holds only while the latest step_running row is fresher than the runner's own liveness horizon; 'waiting on a human' is DELIBERATELY unbounded because a review gate legitimately holds for hours and remains true until someone acts. Pick the freshness window from the producer's heartbeat cadence, not an arbitrary number.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/teams/sub_collab/useTeamChannel.ts` — `PRESENCE_WORK_WINDOW_MS = 10min`: 'without a bound a team whose run died… keeps rendering its roster as "working" forever — the terminal row that would clear it may simply never arrive. Ten minutes matches the runner's own liveness horizon: anything genuinely running emits step traffic well inside it.' `derivePresence` applies the window only to `step_running`; `status_awaiting_review` → waiting with no bound ('WAITING is deliberately unbounded: a review gate legitimately holds for hours'). `deriveLastSeen` starts at the persona's first visible row of ANY kind 'so an agent becomes visible the moment it is spun up, not only when it completes something.'

observed.title: Refcount channel subscriptions and key effect dependencies by value, not array identity
observed.statement: When N surfaces watch the same live feed, route them through one refcounted subscription in the store: the first subscriber triggers the fetch, a shared service keeps every subscribed channel fresh, and each surface releases on unmount — instead of each running its own poll + push listener. In the React hook, join the id array into a string key for the effect dependency because 'callers routinely pass fresh arrays' — subscribing by identity would churn the subscription every render.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/teams/sub_collab/useTeamChannel.ts` — header: 'Subscribing is refcounted: N surfaces watching the same team share one fetch instead of each running its own poll + listener' (state/poll/push consolidated into `channelSlice` + `useChannelService`); `useChannelSubscription` comment 'Subscribe by VALUE, not identity — callers routinely pass fresh arrays' with `teamIds.join(',')` and sorted `kindKey`; `useTeamPresence` reuses the same shared feed ('no separate poll') for presence-only surfaces.

observed.title: Long client polling loops need cooperative cancellation on unmount AND single-owner arbitration
observed.statement: Imperative loops that poll a backend for minutes (reap-until-done, run-to-budget) must check a mountedRef/runningRef pair at every iteration and after every await — otherwise navigation away leaves them polling for up to their full cap (documented: 20 minutes of 2s polls plus a refresh fan-out). When a periodic interval AND an imperative loop can both drive the same recovery call, gate the interval on the loop's busy flag so two owners never call the same operation for the same id concurrently.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/teams/sub_deliberations/useTeamDeliberations.ts` — `mountedRef` comment: 'Without this, approveAction's reap loop kept polling every 2s for up to 20 minutes after the user navigated away… and runToBudget/runAllTracks only stopped on teamId change, not on unmount.' `approveAction`'s loop condition `i < 600 && mountedRef.current && d.status === 'action_running'`; the poll interval skips the reap 'when approveAction's own imperative loop already owns it (actionBusy) — otherwise both loops call pollDeliberationAction for the same id concurrently.' `runAllTracks` advances open tracks with `Promise.all` per round and per-track catches so one failed advance doesn't kill the round. Status sets (`ACTIVE_STATUSES`, `AUTO_ADVANCE_STATUSES`) declare which states poll and which auto-advance.

observed.title: Notification dedupe per entity: reset on state exit, un-mark on failure so retry can renotify
observed.statement: A global listener that notifies on a state transition needs three-part idempotency: (1) mark the entity id on first notify so the orchestrator's duplicate tick-re-entry events don't double-notify; (2) DELETE the mark when the entity leaves the state, so a future re-entry legitimately fires again; (3) on downstream failure while building the notification, delete the mark too — 'so a subsequent event retries the notification instead of being permanently suppressed.' Also handle the async-listen race: if unmount wins before the listen promise resolves, immediately unlisten.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/teams/sub_assignments/useAssignmentNotificationDispatcher.ts` — `notifiedRef` Set with all three moves: mark on `awaiting_review`, `delete` when `status !== 'awaiting_review'` ('so a future re-failure can fire another notification'), and `delete` in the catch ('Undo the dedupe mark so a subsequent awaiting_review event… retries the notification instead of being permanently suppressed'). The mount cleanup pattern: `void listen(...).then((u) => { if (cancelled) u(); else unlisten = u; })` handles the unmount-before-listen-resolves race.

observed.title: Keyset pagination over second-resolution timestamps needs a composite (at, id) cursor
observed.statement: A timestamp-only keyset cursor silently drops rows when a burst shares one second across a page boundary. Make the cursor composite — the last item's timestamp AND id, exclusive — and thread both through the API. Related read-model honesty: push kind filters down into SQL so each source query gets its own limit (a chatty source must not starve others out of a shared union LIMIT), and compute facet counts in SQL because 'the facet rail cannot count rows it never fetched.'
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/api/pipeline/teamChannel.ts` — `ChannelCursor` doc: '`at` alone is only second-resolution, so a burst of rows sharing one second across a page boundary would be dropped; pass the last item's `id` too.' `listTeamChannel` doc: '`kinds` is pushed down into SQL — each source query is limited independently… (Previously all four sources ran with LIMIT n and the union was truncated to n total, so a chatty step layer could starve every memory out of the page.)' `countTeamChannelKinds` doc: deliberation turns are absent from the blended read, so the rail 'was rendering "Deliberation 0" for teams with hundreds of turns. Counting has to happen where the rows are.'

observed.title: Prefer one unfiltered batch call plus client-side filtering over N scoped IPC calls
observed.statement: When a screen needs a cross-entity rollup and the backend command only filters by a single value, one unfiltered list call filtered and grouped client-side beats multiple filtered calls — 'asking twice would double the IPC to save a client-side filter.' The same store collapses per-project fan-out (listScans × N) into one generous-limit batched list grouped client-side, invalidated surgically per project on the events that change it (scoped 20-row re-fetch merged into the cache) rather than re-polled on a timer; a single project's refresh failure logs and leaves the family status alone because 'the rest of the cache is still valid.'
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/lib/sceneStore.ts` — header ('opening Mastermind used to fan out N+1 IPC per project… and relied on a 5s fleet poll… collapses the per-family fetch to ≤1 IPC… invalidates surgically on the events that actually change a project's data'); `loadRunners` comment ('`dev_tools_list_tasks` takes a single status, and the canvas needs two (running AND queued). Asking twice would double the IPC to save a client-side filter'); `SCAN_LIMIT = 500` single list + `groupScansByProject`; `invalidateScans(projectId)` scoped merge with the non-fatal-failure comment. Throttles for remote APIs: `MONITOR_MIN_INTERVAL = 60s`, `LLM_SPEND_MIN_INTERVAL = 5min`, with remembered last inputs for `retryFailed`, and a late `import('./llmSpend')` keeping tracing adapters out of the canvas's first chunk.

observed.title: Bounded per-item remote fan-out where one item's failure means absent-from-map, not family failure
observed.statement: Fetching a live stat per entity from a remote API: run a worker-pool limiter (fixed width, shared cursor) over only the eligible targets, and treat each per-item failure as 'this entity is honestly unknown' — leave it out of the returned map and log — rather than failing the whole batch. Throw only when the operation can't run at all. Consumers then render absent entries with the honest-fallback (static-only) treatment.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/lib/liveState.ts` — `boundedForEach` (width = min(limit, items.length), shared `cursor++` loop) at concurrency 4 over Sentry stat fetches; per-project try/catch: 'One project's stats failing is non-fatal — leave it unknown'; contract comment: 'Projects without a supported credential, or whose per-project fetch fails, are simply absent from the returned map (honest unknown → readiness-only colour). Throws only if it can't run at all.' The module also reuses the Observability tab's Sentry adapter verbatim ('no fork'). The repo has hoisted the same limiter to `@/lib/concurrency` (`sceneStore.ts` re-export note: two features had 'an independent copy of the exact same limiter').

observed.title: Date.now()-only ids collide the moment a second writer or a same-millisecond batch appears
observed.statement: `prefix + Date.now().toString(36)` is unique only while ONE writer creates at most one object per millisecond — an AI agent composing a batch in a single tick while the user is drawing breaks both halves of that assumption. Collision-safe form: base36 millis + per-process wrapping sequence (separates same-millisecond creations within one writer) + random tail (separates writers from each other). Leave existing ids untouched; only shape new ones.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/lib/canvasIds.ts` — the whole module is the lesson: 'The old form was `g${Date.now().toString(36)}` — unique only as long as ONE writer creates at most one object per millisecond. Athena composes a whole batch in a single tick, and she does it while the user is drawing, so both halves of that assumption are gone.' `canvasId(prefix)` = prefix + base36 ms + 4-char base36 seq (mod 36^4) + 4-char random tail.

observed.title: Bridge fire-and-forget eval harnesses with a window global plus a hidden DOM result stash
observed.statement: When a test harness can inject JS but cannot await a promise across calls (fire-and-forget /eval), expose a dev-gated `window.__x.dispatch(action)` that ALSO mirrors every settled result into a hidden DOM node (`data-testid` stash) a later /query call reads back. Gate on `import.meta.env.DEV` so the global never ships; mount/unmount the bridge with the surface it drives so it exists exactly while something can answer.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/lib/canvasTestBridge.ts` — '`/eval`… is fire-and-forget — it cannot await a promise across calls. So this bridge exposes `window.__mmCanvas.dispatch(action)` AND mirrors every settled result into a hidden DOM stash (`data-testid="mm-action-result"`) that a later `/query` call reads back. The established eval→DOM-readback pattern.' Dev gating: '`import.meta.env.DEV` covers tauri:dev:test… and keeps the global out of shipped bundles.' The hook is 'Mounted by CanvasShell — the bridge exists exactly while a shell can answer', with full cleanup (stash removed, global deleted) on unmount.

observed.title: Adapt the per-frame mount budget by measuring the previous wave instead of hardcoding it
observed.statement: When first-mounting a heavy scene in waves (N items per animation frame), the right N is a property of the MACHINE, not the scene — a fixed constant either stalls a busy laptop or wastes frames on a workstation. Time each wave's commit and size the next wave from the result, clamped to [min, max], shrinking when commit time exceeds ~1.5 frames. Pair with viewport culling whose margin covers a whole item footprint so items are only culled once fully clear (no popping).
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/lib/CanvasShell.tsx` — `MOUNT_WAVE_START 4 / MIN 1 / MAX 14`, `MOUNT_FRAME_BUDGET_MS = 24` with the rationale: 'one island is ~150 SVG nodes, and how many of those fit in a frame is a property of the machine, not of the canvas — a fixed 5 either stalls a busy laptop or wastes frames on a workstation. Each wave is timed and the next one is sized from the result.' `CULL_MARGIN = 700` — 'half an island footprint plus slack, so an island is only culled once its whole body is well clear of the viewport — no popping.' `MastermindPage.tsx` `HYDRATE_WAVE = 6` applies the same wave idea to content adoption ('islands allowed to ADOPT changed content per pass').

observed.title: Spatial keyboard navigation: one roving cursor with cone-scored directional picks and a nearest fallback
observed.statement: A spatial map must not become N tab stops ('a 200-project portfolio must not become 200 tab presses') — use one roving cursor and let arrow keys navigate spatially: candidates must sit inside a cone around the direction vector, scored by along-axis distance plus weighted lateral drift so 'right' prefers the item actually beside you over a nearer one off-axis. When the cone is empty, fall back to plain-nearest so a sparse or single-column map can never trap the cursor with no way out. Keep the geometry pure (no React/DOM) so the decision logic is unit-testable.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/lib/kbNav.ts` — `pickInDirection` with `CONE_RATIO = 2`, `PERP_WEIGHT = 2`, and the empty-cone nearest fallback ('a sparse or single-column map can never trap the cursor'); `nearestTo` for map entry. `CanvasShell.tsx` motivation comment: 'the map is spatial, so arrow keys navigate it spatially rather than walking a DOM order that would bear no relation to what the user sees', plus an aria-live `announce` state. Covered by `__tests__/kbNav.test.ts`.

observed.title: Two surfaces answering the same question must call the same predicate module, not fork it
observed.statement: When a second surface (canvas cell) mirrors an affordance that already exists elsewhere (passport wall gear), it must invoke the SAME applicability functions — 'a canvas cell is clickable exactly when its wall row would show a gear' — instead of re-deriving the answer. The mapping layer is thin: the registry names the counterpart row key and resolution kind; the shared predicates decide. Fork-avoidance applies to adapters too: the canvas reuses the Observability tab's Sentry adapter verbatim. Where a mapping was wrong (a cell labelled Database pointed at the migrations row), the fix is recorded in the registry entry as a comment so the correction can't regress silently.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/lib/dimActions.ts` — header: 'asks the SAME applicability logic ImproveCell uses, so a canvas cell is clickable exactly when its wall row would show a gear'; imports `applicableDeployActions`/`applicableStandardsActions`/`connectorSpecFor`/`MODAL_ROWS` from the passport improve modules. `liveState.ts`: 'Reuses the Observability tab's Sentry adapter — no fork.' `dimRegistry.ts` db/monitoring entries carry the mis-mapping postmortems ('pointing its click at the migrations row sent it to a surface about something else'). `MastermindPage.tsx`: KPI dimension reads 'the same rollup the Passport wall's warning badges use — the two surfaces must agree on "off track".'

observed.title: Payloads destined for an LLM transcript are digests: counts not lists, capped lists with an honest +N more
observed.statement: State reported back into an agent's context window must be trimmed at the reporting seam: aggregate lists to counts where names add nothing ('the digest reports "2 live sessions", never names'), and cap enumerations at a small N with an explicit '…+N more' tail — ten plus an honest remainder tells the model the same thing a whole portfolio dump would, at a fraction of the tokens. Do the trimming in the bridge that formats the report, not in the underlying data model.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/lib/useCanvasControlBridge.ts` — `VISIBLE_SLUGS_MAX = 10` and `compactResult`: 'Trim the readback for the transcript: the full visible-slug list can be a whole portfolio; ten plus an honest "+N more" tells her the same thing' (appends the literal `…+N more` entry). `scenePublish.ts` `toProject`: 'Counts, not lists: the digest reports "2 live sessions", never names' (`fleet: island.fleet.length`, `personasRunning: …length`). Also defense-in-depth at the same seam: `STEERING_KINDS` allow-list drops any event-carried action kind the dispatcher shouldn't emit ('an event is an event').

observed.title: Give unattended automation three fire modes: auto, dry-run-suppress-outbound, and hold-for-approval
observed.statement: Triggers that fire without a human present need a per-trigger unattended mode: 'auto' (fire normally), 'dry_run' (run the pipeline but suppress outbound side effects), and 'approval' (hold the fire in a pending queue until a human approves — approval publishes the held event and the run proceeds; rejection discards). The queue is first-class API surface (list pending fires, resolve by id) so any surface can build a review inbox over it.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/api/pipeline/triggers.ts` — `UnattendedMode = 'auto' | 'dry_run' | 'approval'`, `setTriggerUnattendedMode` ('fire normally, run-but-suppress-outbound, or hold for human approval'), `listPendingTriggerFires`, `resolvePendingTriggerFire(id, approved)` ('Approve (publish the held event → the run proceeds) or reject (discard)'). Companion safety valves in the same file: `dryRunTrigger` returning the simulated event + matched subscriptions without firing, and `validateTrigger` for static checks.

observed.title: Rename a shared identifier atomically across every referencing store and return per-store counts
observed.statement: An identifier referenced by several tables and embedded JSON configs (event types in events, subscriptions, trigger configs, persona prompt handler maps) gets renamed through ONE atomic command that: rejects reserved/infrastructure names, rejects collisions anywhere the new name already exists, updates every store in one transaction, and returns per-store update counts so the caller can show exactly what moved. Pair it with an idempotent one-shot cleanup command for the orphan classes that accumulate anyway (dead audit rows, missing auto-listeners).
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/api/pipeline/triggers.ts` — `renameEventType` doc: 'Atomically rename an event type everywhere it's referenced: persona_events, persona_event_subscriptions, persona_triggers.config (event_type / listen_event_type / _handler_key), and personas.structured_prompt.eventHandlers. Rejects reserved infrastructure event types (catalog) and collisions… Returns per-store counts' → `RenameEventTypeResult` with six count fields. `cleanupDeadTriggerEvents` ('Deletes triggers whose owning persona is gone, purges dead trigger_fired audit rows, and backfills missing auto-listeners… Idempotent') returns `TriggerCleanupResult` counts. Same atomic-pairing shape in `linkPersonaToEvent`/`unlinkPersonaFromEvent`: trigger row + prompt handler text created/removed together.

observed.title: Seed schedule previews with the same id the engine hashes so preview and reality agree
observed.statement: When a scheduler expands hash-based tokens (Jenkins-style `H` in cron) using a stable per-trigger seed, every preview surface must accept and pass the SAME seed (the trigger id) — otherwise the preview shows a different minute than the engine will actually fire, and the calendar lies. Syntax-only previews before an id exists may omit the seed; anything shown as 'next runs' must not. Windowed projections carry an explicit backend-capped max.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/api/pipeline/triggers.ts` — `previewCronSchedule` seed param doc: 'Stable id (usually trigger.id) hashed into Jenkins H tokens so the preview matches the minute the engine will actually fire.
