- `mod.rs:435-447` continue-vs-break; test `mod.rs:756-770` `per_kind_cap_does_not_starve_other_kinds`.

observed.title: Write time-window semantics as a numbered contract and pin each clause with a property test
observed.statement: Quiet-hours and cadence evaluators each open with a numbered contract (inclusive start / exclusive end, wrap behavior, whitelist semantics) and carry a prop-test module mapping 1:1 onto the clauses, with a stated rule that a failure updates doc and test together. Cheapest known defense for date/time logic, where all the bugs are boundary bugs.
observed.detail_md:
Evidence:
- `src-tauri/src/companion/proactive/quiet.rs:17-54` (5 clauses) + `quiet.rs:224-389` (`from_eq_to_is_never_quiet`, `boundary_inclusion_same_day`, `wrap_inverts_membership_on_interior_points`, `days_filter_excluding_today_always_blocks`).
- `triggers.rs:20-51` (4 clauses) + `triggers.rs:812-1010` incl. `cadence_never_wraps_midnight`.
- The two contracts deliberately differ (quiet windows wrap midnight, cadences do not) with the rationale written down (`triggers.rs:33-38`).
- Companion decision: ambiguous config resolves toward the quiet failure — `from == to` is zero-length not 24h silence, empty `days: []` matches nothing, unparseable schedule_json is skipped (`quiet.rs:26-45`, `:70-73`).

observed.title: Merge batch LLM verdicts fail-closed: omitted rejects, inexact token rejects, unknown id drops, duplicate ignored
observed.statement: Three independent batch-decision modules converge on one merge discipline: an id the model never returned is rejected (a dropped line must never read as approval), a verdict token that is not exactly the accept literal degrades to reject, hallucinated ids are dropped so they cannot create phantom rows, and duplicate verdicts for one item are ignored after the first (which also prevents a count underflow). An empty sanitized result is an Err so the caller falls back to deterministic composition instead of rendering a stub.
observed.detail_md:
Evidence:
- `src-tauri/src/companion/proactive/backlog_triage.rs:17-22`, `:233-290`; tests `:421-441`.
- `message_triage.rs:336-349` — duplicate verdicts would "make the `batch.len() - touched` below underflow (panic in debug, absurd count in release)".
- `execution_review.rs:779-782` — `checked_sub(1).and_then(|i| groups.get(i)) else { continue; // hallucinated group id }`.
- `brain/briefing.rs:44-74`, `:253-313`, `:344-348` — widget kinds and action kinds on allowlists, action target ids must appear in the input document, empty result => error => deterministic fallback; tests `sanitize_drops_unknown_kinds_actions_and_foreign_ids`.

observed.title: Gate periodic database maintenance on a live-work gauge, not just a timer
observed.statement: Run expensive idle maintenance (PRAGMA optimize, WAL truncate-checkpoint) on a timer, but skip the tick whenever an in-flight-work gauge shows the system is busy, so maintenance never competes with user-facing queries.

Initial 30s delay keeps it out of the boot window. The gauge is the same one the IPC layer already maintains, so the check is free.

observed.title: Register connection-scoped extensions BEFORE the pool exists — they only apply to new connections
observed.statement: SQLite auto-extensions (and any per-connection registration) affect only connections opened after registration; a pool built first holds connections that silently lack the extension, and every query using it fails on exactly those cached connections.

This bites the companion's first-boot ingest … 'no such module: vec0' from any vec query on those connections." `vector_store.rs` wraps registration in a `std::sync::Once` so repeated calls are safe.

observed.title: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS never adds columns — pair every late column with an ignore-error ALTER
observed.statement: On an install that already has the table, `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` with a new column silently skips it — which is every install that matters. Additive columns need a paired `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` where 'duplicate column name' is treated as the success path, ordered before any index that depends on the column.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/db/src/lib.rs` COMPANION_SCHEMA block — `tags_json` is "an ALTER rather than a column in COMPANION_SCHEMA because companion_node is an EXISTING table: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS would silently skip the new column on every install that already has the table, which is all of them." The defensive ALTER loops note "SQLite reports 'duplicate column name' on every run after the first, and that is the success path, not an error." `migrations/initial.rs` runs pre-schema ALTERs before the consolidated SCHEMA "so that indexes on new columns don't fail for existing DBs."

observed.title: Wrap multi-statement DDL in an explicit transaction — SQLite autocommits per statement
observed.statement: A migration batch of CREATE TABLE + CREATE INDEX + data backfill must run inside one BEGIN IMMEDIATE/COMMIT; under SQLite's default per-statement autocommit, a crash or power loss mid-batch leaves half-applied schema that idempotency probes then misread.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/db/src/migrations/incremental.rs` — helper comment: "Wrap a DDL batch in BEGIN IMMEDIATE / COMMIT so multi-statement scripts (CREATE TABLE + CREATE INDEX + INSERT FROM legacy) succeed or roll back as a unit. SQLite's default auto-commit applies per statement, which leaves partial schema state on power-loss or panic mid-batch." Each `IncrementalMigration` also carries an `already_applied` probe, so atomicity is what keeps the probe truthful.

observed.title: Sweep FK orphans at startup even when ON DELETE CASCADE is declared
observed.statement: Declared cascades are necessary but not sufficient: crashed mid-flight runs and repo-bypassing code paths still strand orphan child rows. A one-shot, per-table, best-effort sweep at init cleans accumulated drift, no-ops on healthy installs, and logs per-table counts.

The comment is explicit that cascades SHOULD fire (FK pragma on every pooled connection) yet "We've still observed orphans accumulate in real installs — likely from runs that errored mid-flight … or code paths that bypassed the repo." Per-table errors are logged at debug and skipped (table may not exist on fresh installs); a nonzero total logs at info.

observed.title: Enforce late-added column bounds with ABORT triggers when ALTER cannot add a CHECK
observed.statement: SQLite cannot ALTER a CHECK constraint onto an existing table; instead install BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE triggers that RAISE(ABORT) on out-of-range values, guard the DROP+CREATE behind a triggers-already-present probe (an unconditional recreate is a schema write on every boot), and rename the triggers whenever the body changes so existing DBs pick up the new definition.
