The presence guard comment: "Skip the DROP+CREATE when both triggers already exist — the re-create was an unconditional sqlite_master/journal WRITE on every app boot. NOTE: if you change the trigger bodies below, also change the trigger names (or delete this guard for one release)."

observed.title: Seed vocabularies with INSERT OR IGNORE so re-seeding cannot resurrect operator changes; demote by status, never delete
observed.statement: Boot-time seed rows keyed on a UNIQUE natural key via INSERT OR IGNORE are idempotent AND respect later human/agent edits: because the row already exists, re-running cannot reset a status someone changed. Removal is a status demotion, not a DELETE — a deleted seed row would silently reappear on the next boot.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/db/src/lib.rs` `companion_taxonomy` seed block — "INSERT OR IGNORE keyed on the UNIQUE tag … cannot resurrect the *status* of a tag a cycle or the operator has since changed, because the row already exists and the insert is skipped entirely. Deleting a seed row does re-seed it on the next boot; demote by status instead of deleting." The table itself embodies the companion design bet that "schema evolution is rows, never DDL": new classifications arrive as gated 'proposed' rows, not enum edits.

observed.title: Stage inbound sync deltas in an inbox table that exactly one reconciler consumes
observed.statement: Cross-device (or cross-system) sync should never force-write long-term state. Land every arriving delta in a staging inbox tagged with its origin; a single scheduled reconciler is the only consumer, treats rows as semi-trusted evidence through the same dedupe/supersede machinery as local writes, and marks consumption with the consumer-run id (NULL = unprocessed) instead of deleting — giving idempotent redelivery and an audit trail for free.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/db/src/lib.rs` `companion_sync_inbox` — the schema comment states the contract: "LS **writes** here … The sleep cycle's **reconcile phase is the ONLY consumer** … **Sync never force-writes long-term memory.** Conflict resolution IS the sleep cycle; this table is what makes that possible instead of aspirational." `processed_cycle_id` records WHICH run consumed each row ("a bad reconcile is auditable rather than merely regrettable"); rows are never deleted on processing. Partial index `idx_companion_sync_inbox_unprocessed` keys the consumer's scan.

observed.title: Journal reversible writes as before-images through an allowlisted preupdate hook — and exclude tables where undo is a hazard
observed.statement: For agent-write reversibility, capture INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on a curated table allowlist via the database's preupdate hook, persisting before-images (never after-images) through a bounded channel to a dedicated writer. Exclude the journal table itself (recursion), run records (undo must not erase evidence a run happened), and credentials (undo resurrecting a revoked secret is a security hazard). Store values as-persisted so encrypted columns journal ciphertext, and count channel-full drops as permanent, loudly-logged audit gaps.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/db/src/journal.rs` — `JOURNAL_TABLES` allowlist with per-exclusion rationale (`change_journal` recursion guard re-checked in `is_journaled_table`; `persona_executions` "undoing a run must not erase the evidence that the run happened"; `persona_credentials` "resurrecting revoked credentials via undo is a security hazard"). Invariants block: hook does no I/O, only an owned copy + non-blocking send; "Ciphertext only … nothing in this module ever decrypts"; `note_journal_drop` warns on first drop ("a permanent gap in the reversibility ledger") then every 1000th.

observed.title: Stamp ambient write-attribution via task-local plus thread-scope RAII, readable inside database hooks
observed.statement: When a synchronous hook deep in the data layer must know 'which execution caused this write' without threading a parameter through every layer, provide two ambient scopes: a tokio task-local wrapper around the whole run future (visible from any sync code polled by the task) and a thread-scoped RAII guard for spawn_blocking paths. Readers check task scope first, then thread scope, and return None for ordinary user writes — and the known gap (out-of-process writers see no hooks) is documented as an accepted limitation rather than papered over.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/db/src/attribution.rs` — `with_execution` (tokio `task_local!`) + `ThreadAttributionGuard` (RAII fallback), consumed by the preupdate hook in `journal.rs` (`execution_id` stamped AT CAPTURE TIME on the writing thread). The module doc names the shape ("pass context downward without layer inversion") and states the v1 limitation: `personas-mcp` attaching via `open_pool_at` runs "in a different process with no hooks installed and [its writes] are neither journaled nor attributed."

observed.title: Pair every settings key with a _DEFAULT constant and encode the unit in the key name
observed.statement: A settings-key registry should ship each key with a sibling `<KEY>_DEFAULT` constant — so 'what does unset mean?' has exactly one answer codebase-wide — and encode units in the key name itself (`_DAYS`, `_MS`), with the rule that renaming the unit means renaming the key.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/db/src/settings_keys.rs` module doc: "Every key defined here is paired with a `<KEY>_DEFAULT` constant … Consumers MUST reference the `_DEFAULT` constant rather than hard-coding a literal, so that 'what does unset mean for this key?' has exactly one answer. Units are encoded in the key name itself (`_DAYS`, `_MS`, ...) — do not rename a key without also changing the unit." `validate_key`/`validate_value` are enforced inside `repos::core::settings::set` so internal callers cannot bypass them.

observed.title: Instrument pool acquires with a labeled starvation threshold, and convert acquire hangs into recoverable errors
observed.statement: Give the connection pool a hard acquire timeout (a frozen worker becomes a recoverable error instead of a hung UI) and a drop-in instrumented acquire that logs caller label, wait time, and pool state whenever a successful acquire exceeded a tuned starvation threshold — so pool contention is visible in production logs, swappable at hot paths without other changes.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/db/src/lib.rs` — `POOL_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT` (5s): "the user gets a recoverable error rather than a frozen UI"; `acquire_logged(pool, label)` warns past `POOL_STARVATION_WARN_MS` (250ms, "tuned to catch the 'vector_kb search holding a connection while concurrent IPC reads pile up' scenario") including `idle`/`total` pool state, and errors with wait time on acquire failure. Doc: "Functionally identical to pool.get(); safe to swap in at hot paths … Cold paths can keep using pool.get() directly."

observed.title: Assert cross-table data invariants at startup — loud error log, never a crash
observed.statement: After migrations, run cheap SQL assertions of the invariants your migration chain is supposed to guarantee (e.g. 'no row holds both the legacy blob and the new field rows'). Log violations at error level with the offending ids for forensics, but do not abort boot — a transient inconsistency during a future migration may be acceptable, while a silent one regresses undetected.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/db/src/migrations/helpers.rs::assert_credential_blob_invariant` — one EXISTS query for rows with `encrypted_data <> ''` AND field rows; on hits: `tracing::error!(count, credential_ids, "credential blob invariant violated … credential_fields is the source of truth and the blob columns must be empty")`. The doc comment states the posture explicitly: "it does not crash the app … but every breach is captured for forensic review."

observed.title: Gate a session-open LLM briefing on a computed delta — quiet means no model call
observed.statement: Before firing an LLM to compose a 'while you were away' briefing, build a serializable delta document from data already on hand and run a triviality gate over it. A trivial delta renders an honest deterministic 'quiet night' state with zero model calls and no navigation hijack; only a real delta spends the LLM, and even then a deterministic fallback composition (same widget vocabulary) covers null/failed responses so the surface never degrades to an error.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/home/sub_cockpit/briefing/useMorningBriefing.ts` — first run (no anchor) does nothing; `deltaIsTrivial(delta)` → `composeQuietBriefing` with `composedBy: 'quiet'` and explicitly no `setHomeTab('cockpit')`; only a real delta calls `companionComposeBriefing` and navigates. `sessionDelta.ts` documents that the client gate mirrors Rust `briefing::delta_is_trivial` ("When true, NO compose IPC fires") and that open incidents deliberately don't re-trigger a briefing every launch. On compose failure/null, `composeFallbackBriefing(delta, labels)` emits the same `stat_grid`/`issue_list`/`verdict` widget kinds and the same action enum the LLM path is allowed to emit, and the banner labels provenance (`athena` / `fallback` / `quiet`).

observed.title: LLM-composed widgets carry only enum actions — validated twice, capped, confirmed when spendy, audited
observed.statement: When a model composes UI that includes one-click actions, the actions are a closed discriminated union (never free-form), validated server-side against the source document AND re-parsed client-side at render time (unknown kinds and missing targets silently dropped, count capped), with a confirm dialog for spendy/destructive kinds, and every execution recorded to an audit ledger as a best-effort follow-up that cannot fail the action itself.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/home/sub_cockpit/briefing/actionTypes.ts` — `CockpitWidgetAction` is a 4-variant union; `parseWidgetActions` drops malformed entries and caps at `MAX_WIDGET_ACTIONS = 3` ("Mirrors the Rust cap"; backend mirror named: `src-tauri/src/companion/brain/briefing.rs` `ACTION_KINDS` + `action_allowed_on`); `actionNeedsConfirm` names rerun/pause as the spendy set. `CockpitPanel.tsx` re-parses at render: "never trust a stored/composed spec's raw shape". `actions.ts` `runWidgetAction` executes via existing IPC, throws the IPC error to the caller, then writes the decision-ledger row with `.catch(silentCatch(...))` — "acting must not fail because the audit write couldn't land". `WidgetActionBar.tsx` implements one-click + confirm + per-button idle/busy/done/failed state.

observed.title: Read the previous session's watermark in a render-time initializer — child effects advance it before parent effects run
observed.statement: When a surface both consumes a persisted last-seen watermark and advances it on a heartbeat, freeze the previous-session value in a `useState` lazy initializer during the FIRST render. React runs child effects before parent effects, so a parent that reads the watermark in its own effect gets the value a child heartbeat already overwrote. Pair this with a module-scoped once-per-session latch (surviving remounts, reset on reload) plus an exported test-only reset.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/home/sub_cockpit/briefing/useMorningBriefing.ts` — `const [anchor] = useState(() => (briefingRan ? null : readLastSeen()))` with the comment "child effects (the Welcome heartbeat) advance the stored value before any parent effect gets to run"; module-level `let briefingRan = false` latch + `__resetMorningBriefingForTests()`. Same freeze idiom in `sub_welcome/lib/sinceLeftBriefing.ts` `useSinceLeftBriefing` (`useState(() => readLastSeen())`) whose heartbeat writes the anchor every 60s and on `beforeunload`/hide.

observed.title: A fetch-if-empty guard keyed on the empty result loops forever — latch the request in a ref
observed.statement: `useEffect(() => { if (list.length === 0) fetch(); }, [list])` is an infinite loop on genuinely-empty data: every fetch of an empty collection produces a fresh `[]` identity, which re-produces the guard state. Latch 'already requested' in a one-shot ref instead. Sibling trap: keying an unrelated fetch on a refetched array's identity re-runs it on every rename/background refresh — fetch once on mount if the data doesn't actually depend on the array.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/home/sub_cockpit/CockpitPanel.tsx` — `personasRequestedRef` with comment "An empty fleet re-produces the guard state (fresh [] identity per fetch), which looped fetchPersonas for as long as the panel was open on a zero-persona install"; identical fix duplicated in `widgets/PersonaOverviewWidget.tsx`. The sibling trap in the same file: metrics effect deliberately `[]`-dependent — "Keying this on `personas` refetched the summary on every fleet-array identity change (renames, background refreshes)".

observed.title: The storage event never fires in the writing window — pair persisted markers with an in-process subscriber list
observed.statement: In a single-window shell (Tauri/Electron), relying on the `storage` event to observe a localStorage marker is dead code: the event fires only in OTHER windows/tabs, never in the writer. Keep the marker in localStorage for reload survival, but layer a tiny module-level subscriber Set on top so live components re-read on every write — and document which signals are the ONLY re-read triggers, so nobody re-adds a proxy dependency (like array length) that misses same-entity repeat writes.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/home/sub_welcome/useResumeContext.ts` — `editListeners: Set<EditListener>` + `subscribeLastEdited`/`notifyLastEditedChange` with the full rationale comment; `markPersonaEdited`/`clearLastEdited` persist then notify. The documented invariant: "We do NOT key off `personas.length` (the old behavior), because editing the same persona twice in a row leaves the count stable and would surface a stale name."

observed.title: Surface one ranked resume signal, never a list — priority-ordered kinds with null meaning render nothing
observed.statement: A 'continue where you left off' affordance should resolve to at most ONE signal via an explicit priority ladder over a typed union (e.g. fresh failure > paused guided flow > last edit), returning null when nothing clears the bar so the surface renders nothing rather than filler. Within a rank, pick the most recent explicitly (sort, not `find()`, when source order is unguaranteed) and clamp future-dated timestamps from clock skew before age checks. Each kind carries its own dismiss semantics.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/home/sub_welcome/useResumeContext.ts` — `ResumeContext` union with documented ranking; failure branch maps/sorts by parsed timestamp with `Math.max(0, now - ts)` clamp and the comment that `find()` "would return whichever happened to be first in the array"; tour branch only fires when paused (so it never duplicates the live panel); age windows per kind (24h failures, 7d edits). `ResumeBanner.tsx` — one-click jump per kind; dismiss clears the localStorage marker for edits, `dismissTour()` for tours, and documents that failures have no per-execution ack today.

observed.title: A red fleet indicator needs both a minimum terminal sample and a strict-majority ratio
observed.statement: A user-facing 'failure spike' alarm should fire only when BOTH hold: the terminal sample (completed+failed, excluding in-flight and cancelled) meets a minimum count, AND failures are a strict majority of finished runs. Either alone is noise: a single bad run on a quiet morning paints the fleet red; a large sample at exactly 50% is ambiguous. Capture thresholds as named exported constants with per-constant rationale and a boundary-behavior table, and state the denominator doctrine at module top so every ratio in the file shares it.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/home/sub_welcome/lib/fleetHealth.ts` — module-level DENOMINATOR note ("5 completed + 5 running would read '50%' instead of the honest '100% of finished runs'"); `FAILURE_SPIKE_MIN_EXECUTIONS = 3` ("the smallest sample where a 'majority failed' verdict has any signal value"); `FAILURE_SPIKE_RATIO_THRESHOLD = 0.5` with strict `>`; documented boundary table including `completed=3, failed=3 → false (ratio exactly 0.5)`. `fleetSuccessRatePct` returns `null` over zero terminal runs so callers render '—', not a confident 0%/100%. Reused by `sub_cockpit/defaultCockpit.ts` `successIntent`.

observed.title: Buffer every wizard step as a draft and commit atomically on Finish — X must mean Cancel
observed.statement: In a multi-step stepper modal over persisted profile state, NO step may write the store on click. All steps buffer local drafts and Finish commits them atomically; dismissal (X / Escape) discards drafts. Half-buffered designs (some steps instant-write, some buffered) silently corrupt the saved profile when a user opens the stepper to compare options and dismisses. Also re-sync each draft from the store when the store changes externally, so a stale draft can't overwrite an externally-updated value on save.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/home/sub_welcome/SetupCards.tsx` `SetupStepper` — `roleDraft`/`toolDraft`/`goalDraft` with the incident comment: "Previously, RoleStep and ToolStep wrote `setSetupRole` / `setSetupTool` instantly on click while only `goalDraft` buffered… would silently corrupt their saved profile with a half-edit — there was no Cancel semantics." Commit happens only in `goNext()` at step 2 ("Commit all three drafts atomically on Finish"). Three `useEffect`s re-sync drafts from `setupRole`/`setupTool`/`setupGoal`: "an externally-updated value would silently get overwritten by the stale draft on save."

observed.title: In a tiered fallback fetch, report error only when every tier failed — and stamp which tier served
observed.statement: When a list loads through a preferred source with a fallback source, capture each tier's error separately and classify the final state precisely: results → loaded (stamped with the serving tier for diagnostics); no results with at least one tier succeeding → genuinely empty; error only when EVERY tier threw. Collapsing these makes a flaky network look like an empty catalog (dead-end UI) or an empty catalog look broken. Emit the (phase, source) pair as a metric so the funnel is observable.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/onboarding/components/useOnboardingState.ts` — `getTrendingTemplates` → `listDesignReviews` fallback with separate `trendingErr`/`fallbackErr`; `phase: 'error'` only when `trendingErr && fallbackErr`, else `'empty'`; `source: 'trending' | 'fallback' | null` retained in `TemplateLoadState`; `countTemplateLoad(phase, source)` Sentry metric. Rationale comment: "first-run users on a flaky network see a recoverable error state instead of a disabled button with no explanation" — the error phase drives a Retry button via `templateReloadNonce`.

observed.title: Creation flows must return the created id — never infer 'the newest row is mine'
observed.statement: When a wizard/subflow creates an entity the parent flow must continue with, thread the created id through the completion callback explicitly. Inferring the created entity by max(created_at) is racy against concurrent creates and server-clock drift. After receiving the id, awaiting the list refresh is best-effort: the id alone is enough to render a minimal fallback, so a failed refresh must not abort the flow.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/onboarding/components/useOnboardingState.ts` `handleAdoptionComplete(personaId)` — "Explicit ID from the adoption wizard — no more guessing the newest persona by created_at (which was racy against concurrent creates and server-clock drift)"; `fetchPersonas()` awaited in try/`silentCatch` with "Failures here are non-fatal — we still have the ID and can render a minimal fallback", then `setOnboardingStep('execute')` unconditionally. `OnboardingOverlay.tsx` passes the same id into `AdoptionWizardModal`'s `onPersonaCreated`.

observed.title: A delayed navigation side effect must re-validate the route it assumed before landing
observed.statement: Deep links and guided flows that set a section first and its sub-tab on a short timeout (so the section can mount) must re-check, inside the timeout callback, that the user is still where the scheduler assumed — still on the routed section, still on the scheduling step. Otherwise a stale timer yanks the user to a tab of a screen they already left. Use defense in depth: clear pending timeouts on state change AND re-check inside each callback, so a missed clear still can't misfire.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/home/sub_learning/powerMoves/launchPowerMove.ts` — `SUB_TAB_DELAY_MS = 120` with `if (s.sidebarSection !== nav.section) return;` ("Applying the sub-tab then would yank them to a tab of a section they already left"). `src/features/onboarding/components/GuidedTour.tsx` — `scheduleStepTimeout` re-checks `tourCurrentStepIndex !== stepIndex` inside every queued effect, labeled "Defense-in-depth alongside the navigate effect's clear-on-step-change"; `pendingTimeouts` Set cleared on step change, dismissal and unmount; all scheduled callbacks also bail when `!tourActiveRef.current`.

observed.title: Seed cosmetic variety from a stable hash plus the date, not Math.random
observed.statement: For a rotating cosmetic choice (hero background, accent variant), derive the pick from `hash(stableUserKey) + dayOfYear()` modulo the option count instead of Math.random. The user still gets variety (new day → new look) but the choice is stable within a day, which removes per-mount flicker on theme toggles, HMR reloads, and navigation back to the surface. A tiny FNV-1a is enough — the hash needs stability, not cryptography.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/home/sub_welcome/HeroHeader.tsx` — inline FNV-1a `hashString`, `dayOfYear()`, and `BG_OPTIONS[seed % BG_OPTIONS.length]` inside a `useMemo`, with the comment: "Deterministic background: same user, same day → same hero. New day → fresh look. Removes per-mount flicker on theme toggle, HMR reload, and navigation back to Home that the previous Math.random() introduced."

observed.title: Read a heavy store from a light surface via lazy import plus manual subscribe
observed.statement: When a lightweight always-mounted surface needs a small slice of a heavy feature store, dynamically import the store inside an effect: seed local state from whatever the store already cached, trigger the store's fetch only when the cache is empty, and stay subscribed with an identity-compare so updates flow live. This keeps the heavy store off the surface's eager bundle and — by making the store the single source — collapses duplicate data paths (the old code ran a parallel 30s IPC poll for the same rows).
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/home/sub_welcome/lib/useVaultCredentials.ts` — `import('@/stores/vaultStore')` inside `useEffect` with a `cancelled` flag; `setCreds(s.credentials)` seed; `if (s.credentials.length === 0) s.fetchCredentials()`; `useVaultStore.subscribe` with `prev` identity compare; docblock: "Previously FleetHealthStrip issued its own `list_credentials` IPC on a 30s poll while the nav hook read the store — two sources for the same data; this collapses them to one." Consumed by `useNavCardStatus` for the external/built-in split.

observed.title: Label a display-only heuristic that shadows a canonical classifier, and make its misses harmless
observed.statement: When the canonical classification lives server-side and isn't exposed where a small UI count needs it, a local heuristic (name set + prefix regex) is acceptable ONLY if its docblock names the canonical model, states it is display-only and not a gate, and the miss mode is harmless by construction (an unmatched item lands in the default bucket; nothing breaks). Record that earlier allowlists were deliberately retired so nobody 'fixes' the heuristic back into a readiness gate.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/home/sub_welcome/lib/connectorScope.ts` — docblock names the backend `ConnectorClass` (`zero_config | credential | global_probe`) as canonical, states "this is intentionally NOT a readiness gate — it's a small, best-effort label for a dashboard count", notes the retired `BUILTIN_LOCAL_CONNECTORS` allowlists, and defines the miss mode: "A new local connector that isn't matched here simply shows up in the 'external' bucket; nothing breaks." Implementation is a known-name Set + `/^(personas_|local_)/` prefix test.

observed.title: Interpret ratio-vs-percent by magnitude before scaling, clamp, and flag genuine overflow
observed.statement: A 0–1 ratio rendered as `round(x*100)%` double-scales when a legacy row or model-composed spec stored the value already as a percent (83.11 → '8311%'). Guard at render time: value ≤ 1 → genuine ratio → ×100; value > 1 → already-percent signature → use as-is; clamp to [0,100] and return an explicit overflow flag when the interpreted percentage still exceeds 100, so the caller shows a 'clamped' treatment + tooltip instead of a silently wrong number. Fixing at read means old stored data displays sanely without a migration.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/home/sub_cockpit/widgets/personaStats.ts` `trustPercent` — full docblock tells the 8311% story ("A stale or Athena-composed spec (or a legacy DB row) that stored the score already-scaled… then double-scaled to a nonsense '8311%'"), returns `{ pct, overflow }`, floors non-finite/negative to 0.

observed.title: Pause a persisted surface's refresh loop while a transient overlay owns it
observed.statement: When a transient overlay (contextual view, briefing) is projected over a surface that normally fetches persisted state on mount + window focus, the fetch/refresh loop must be suspended for the overlay's lifetime — otherwise a background refetch clobbers the overlay with older persisted content. The event that publishes NEW persisted content explicitly drops the overlay and refetches, encoding 'persisted just changed → overlay is obsolete'. Dismissing the overlay restores the persisted view untouched.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/home/sub_cockpit/CockpitPanel.tsx` — the load effect starts with `if (contextualCockpit) return;` ("skip the persistent fetch + focus-refresh so the contextual widgets aren't clobbered by an older LLM-composed spec coming back from the backend"); the `COMPANION_COMPOSE_COCKPIT_EVENT` handler does `setContextualCockpit(null); load();` ("compose_cockpit means 'look at the persistent cockpit I just built for you'"). `useMorningBriefing.ts` rides the same `contextualCockpit` mechanism "so dismissing it restores the persistent cockpit untouched".

observed.title: Steps with no detectable action complete on explicit acknowledgement, never a timer
observed.statement: In a guided flow, steps whose completion is a real app event auto-complete on that event; purely informational steps (look at a dashboard, watch a stream) must complete on an explicit 'I've explored this' button — never a hidden timer. Which steps are acknowledgement-style is declared as data (a listed set of completion-event keys), so adding one is a registry edit and the panel renders the button automatically.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/onboarding/components/TourPanelBody.tsx` — `requiresAcknowledge = isExplorationTourEvent(currentStep.completeOn)`; `GenericStepContent` renders the acknowledge button only while `requiresAcknowledge && !isStepCompleted`. `src/features/onboarding/README.md` codifies it: "If the step is purely informational… add the key to `EXPLORATION_TOUR_EVENTS` in `tourSlice.ts`. The panel will render an 'I've explored this' button so the user advances when they're ready (no hidden timer)." The not-yet-done Next button is deliberately styled as secondary 'Skip step' so acknowledging/acting stays the primary path.

observed.title: Migrate flow progress across tier variants through shared step ids
observed.statement: When the same guided flow ships in two tier variants (full vs simple), give the overlapping steps identical ids in both registries and, on tier switch, mark any step completed in one variant as completed in the other. Migration is one-directional per activation (into the newly-started variant) and leaves the other variant's persisted progress untouched, so a tier flip-flop loses no work in either direction.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/onboarding/README.md` §"Tier-switch policy for the active tour" — `getting-started` ↔ `getting-started-simple` share `appearance-setup`, `credentials-intro`, `persona-creation`; "any step the user has already completed in one tour is marked complete in the other… The 'other' tour's persisted progress is left alone so a tier flip-flop doesn't lose work either way." Policy is encoded in `tourSlice.ts::startTour` (outside this territory; the README in-scope is the contract).

observed.title: Validate selector fragments at the mouth of a fire-and-forget async helper
observed.statement: A helper that interpolates a caller-supplied fragment into `querySelector` and runs as fire-and-forget async (nobody awaits or catches it) turns one stray quote/bracket into an invisible SyntaxError — the rejection vanishes. Validate the fragment against a strict pattern at function entry and bail with a console.warn, even when every known caller passes hand-audited literals; keep the pattern local (duplicated, with a comment naming its mirrors) rather than importing a store slice into a DOM utility.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/home/sub_learning/powerMoves/flashSpotlight.ts` — `TESTID_PATTERN = /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$/` with the comment: "Defense-in-depth: every known caller (`registry.ts`) already supplies a hand-audited literal, but a stray quote/bracket must never reach querySelector and throw a SyntaxError inside this fire-and-forget async function, whose rejection nobody awaits or catches"; the pattern is deliberately a local copy of `tourSlice`'s `TOUR_TEST_ID_PATTERN` to keep the file store-free. Mirrored gate `isSafeTourTestId` guards the same interpolation in `TourPanelBody.tsx` `focusHighlight`.

observed.title: A build-acceleration cache must never be able to fail the build
observed.statement: Wiring a compilation cache (sccache, remote cache) as an unconditional wrapper makes the cache's availability a build dependency: a cache-backend outage kills every compile before it starts. Probe the cache's health in a dedicated step and enable the wrapper only on success — degrade to a slow build with a warning, never to no build.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — both `rust-tests` and `binding-drift` jobs deliberately do NOT set `RUSTC_WRAPPER` at job level ("Setting it at job level makes it un-overridable") and instead run 'Enable sccache only if it actually works': `if sccache --start-server && sccache --show-stats; then echo "RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache" >> $GITHUB_ENV; else ::warning …"the gate still runs"; fi`. The comment records the incident: a GHA cache outage "took the entire Rust gate offline from 2026-07-27 onward — all three platforms plus binding-drift — and a test-compilation regression reached master during the blackout."

observed.title: A CI gate that dies before its verdict has never gated anything — audit that each gate actually runs
observed.statement: CI steps fail in ways that look like enforcement but check nothing: a step that errors before reaching its assertion, a command masked with `|| true`, a flag omission that silently skips the surface under test, or a trigger that never fires on the real development flow. Periodically verify each gate has produced a genuine red at least once, and treat 'this step has never actually run' as a distinct bug class.
observed.detail_md: Evidence, all from `.github/workflows/ci.yml` comments documenting real occurrences: (1) commit-lint's `origin/${{ github.base_ref }}..HEAD` expanded to `origin/..HEAD` on push events and "died with fatal: ambiguous argument … it failed with a git error, not a verdict" on every push; (2) `cargo test` without `--features desktop` aborted at the tauri build script, "so this step has never actually run a test"; (3) binding regen was once wrapped in `2>/dev/null || true`, "which silently masked Rust-side breakage"; (4) `--manifest-path` without `--workspace` meant ~200 `#[ts(export)]` types in `personas-core` "are never regenerated here, so the gate silently stops covering the majority of the binding surface"; (5) the workflow header: pull_request-only CI "never ran on the real flow" because development lands directly on master — push:master had to become the primary trigger.

observed.title: Scan for leaked secrets at pre-commit — CI catching a leak is already a leak
observed.statement: Run a secret scanner over staged changes in the pre-commit hook, because a credential that reaches the remote is compromised even if CI rejects the push. When the scanner is an optional local install, wrap it so absence degrades to a skip-with-install-hint — the wrapper must never break a commit and never mutate the tree.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `lefthook.yml` `gitleaks-staged` job → `node scripts/secret-scan.mjs`, with the rationale in-file: "the shift-left D9 control: a leaked key is blocked BEFORE it leaves the machine (CI catching it is already a leak). Runs gitleaks if installed, else skips with an install hint (the wrapper never breaks a commit). Read-only; never mutates the tree." Sits inside a hook file whose design principles forbid stashing/rewriting the tree (concurrent CLI sessions share it).

observed.title: Unchecked mirrors of the real gates — a second CI pipeline, contributor docs — rot into contradicting them
observed.statement: Any hand-maintained mirror of an enforced pipeline (a parallel CI config for another forge, a CONTRIBUTING guide restating the checks) decays silently: fixes land in the primary and never propagate, until the mirror actively teaches the pre-fix behavior. Either machine-check the mirror against the primary, or delete it and link to the one source of truth.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `.gitlab-ci.yml` (the declared "parallel CI option") still runs `cargo test … export_bindings 2>/dev/null || true` — the exact silent-mask `.github/workflows/ci.yml` removed with a comment explaining why — and its `cargo test`/binding jobs lack the `--features desktop` and `--workspace` flags the GitHub pipeline needed to test anything at all, so the mirror re-created every fixed hole. `CONTRIBUTING.md` tells contributors to add i18n keys to `src/i18n/en.ts` (now a back-compat shim; the source is `locales/en.json`) and to "**not** add to non-English locale files" — the exact behavior the `i18n-no-gaps` pre-commit hook in `lefthook.yml` now blocks.

observed.title: Route all codegen through one runner wired into the build's own pre-hooks
observed.statement: Every generated artifact (seeds, checksums, locale splits, binding regen, environment self-healing) should be invoked from a single runner script attached to the package manager's pre-hooks (predev/prebuild, pre<task>), so 'run the app' is the only ritual. A second registration point — a bundler buildStart plugin, an ad-hoc npm script — both duplicates cost and silently diverges when a new task is added to only one list.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `package.json` — `predev`/`prebuild` → `scripts/run-codegen.mjs`; five `pretauri:*` hooks all funnel through `scripts/ensure-ort-cache.mjs` so the ORT arch-mismatch fix is self-healing on every dev/build entry point. `vite.config.ts` records the failure mode of the second owner: "The earlier catalog-codegen buildStart plugin re-ran 4 of those scripts redundantly on every vite build, costing ~600ms per dev start AND silently diverging when a script was added to buildStart only (e.g., agent-icon-sprites never made it into run-codegen.mjs until 2026-05-10). Removed 2026-05-10."

observed.title: Deps imported only by lazy routes must be pre-bundled in dev, or first navigation 504s
observed.statement: With dev-server dependency pre-bundling (Vite optimizeDeps), a package imported exclusively from a lazily-loaded route is first discovered when the user navigates there; the server kicks off a re-optimization mid-session and the in-flight dynamic import fails ('Outdated Optimize Dep' 504). List such deps in the explicit include set so they join the initial optimize pass.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `vite.config.ts` `optimizeDeps.include` — the whole `@xterm/*` stack, with the comment: "xterm + its addons are imported only from the lazily-loaded Fleet chunks … without this Vite first *discovers* them when the user navigates to Fleet, kicks off an on-the-fly dep re-optimization, and 504s ('Outdated Optimize Dep') the in-flight dynamic import of FleetGridPage." Includes the maintenance rule: add any new `@xterm/addon-*` here too, and clear `node_modules/.vite` if a running server cached the old optimize.

observed.title: Grade lint boundaries by maturity: hard error at the mandatory seam, warn plus a dated inventory of known violations at aspirational seams
observed.statement: Not every architectural boundary can be an error on day one. Enforce the non-negotiable seam at error severity; for boundaries with known legacy violations, set the rule to warn AND record in the config itself which files violate it, as of when, and where they should migrate — so the warning stays a tracked debt instead of ambient noise, and can be promoted to error when the inventory empties.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `eslint.config.js` — three tiers of `no-restricted-imports`: app-wide raw `invoke` ban at **error** (with the full why in the message: timeout protection, IPC metrics, idempotency dedup, typed CommandName); `src/features/shared/**` Tauri-runtime ban at **warn** with the inventory inline: "Set to warn for now — there are 3 known violations as of 2026-05-01 (HealingToast, TitleBar, Sidebar) … those should be migrated to feature modules opportunistically"; `shared/components/**` catalog boundary at **warn**, explicitly labeled "ADVISORY … not a build gate" with a pointer to the curation doc. Each message names the fix destination, not just the prohibition.

observed.title: After an in-place multi-entry hydration, assert no un-transformed stubs survive before reporting success
observed.statement: When a transform mutates a list of entries in place (expanding refs/stubs into full content), a mid-list failure leaves earlier entries transformed and later ones as raw stubs — and downstream normalization will happily map those stubs to empty-but-valid records. Defend twice: propagate the transform error as fatal (naming the offending entry id), AND run a post-condition scan that fails the whole operation if any stub survived, so a partial transform can never be reported as success.

observed.title: Never mutate an integrity-checked payload — thread customizations through a parallel channel
observed.statement: When a payload is verified against a checksum/signature at the top of a flow, later steps must not 'conveniently' inject user customizations by editing that payload before the check — the check would reject it, and weakening the check to allow it guts the integrity guarantee. Instead thread overrides as a separate argument that downstream steps merge after verification, leaving the verified bytes untouched.

observed.title: Guard a derived-score history's integrity: append only real changes, and never fold a new dimension into the composite retroactively
observed.statement: A locally recorded time series of a derived score is only trustworthy if (a) a snapshot is appended only when the readings actually changed — so merely opening the surface never inflates the trend — and (b) newly shipped scored dimensions are deliberately left OUT of the composite at first, because folding a new term in would step-change every subject's score at once and the history would render that as real movement. Ship the dimension visible but unweighted; weight it in a change that says so.

observed.title: Judge a simulation channel by pairing each sim point with its nearest real point and trending the normalized gap
observed.statement: When one measurement channel is ground truth and another is a prediction of it (simulated env, forecast, shadow deployment), express credibility as a per-sim-point gap against the nearest-in-time truth point, normalized by the metric's target span. Never invent a pairing (no truth data → explicit 'insufficient', not a gap of 0); flag a truth partner older than the sim point as STALE (the honest move is a re-measure, not a verdict); and only call a converging/diverging direction with ≥2 normalizable runs separated by an epsilon threshold.

observed.title: Back every consequential action with a consent catalog: impact class, ordered steps, standing boundaries — fed live data so the copy is true of THIS run
observed.statement: Actions that spawn agents or write to a user's repo deserve more than a tooltip. Keep a declarative catalog per action: an impact class (read / write / agent), the ordered steps the click actually sets off, the boundaries that hold no matter what, and at-a-glance facts (scope, engine, duration, what it writes). Two disciplines make it honest: the catalog carries an explicit same-edit contract ('everything here must stay TRUE of the code paths — if a flow changes, change its steps in the same edit'), and run-specific data is passed in late so the consent copy describes what THIS project's run would do, falling back to generic copy only before the data loads.

observed.title: Grade maturity against an explicit rubric with archetype-scaled targets, not one absolute bar
observed.statement: Replace magic numbers buried in score weights with a rubric-as-data: each dimension declares a weight, a pure accessor for current attainment (0..1 position on that dimension's ladder), and a per-archetype TARGET (solo < team < org). The score is the weighted % of targets met given the subject's own archetype — so a solo prototype isn't held to an org-grade bar, and the bar itself is reviewable and tunable in one table instead of scattered through the scoring code.

observed.title: Rank remediation by impact-per-effort — score lift ÷ action cost tier — and drop gaps with no executable action
observed.statement: Turn a diagnostic scorecard into a work queue by scoring every below-target gap as the composite-% it would unlock (dimension weight × remaining gap ÷ total weight) divided by an effort tier for the fixing lever (config toggle < automated scan < wiring a connector < an agent task). Map each dimension to its lever in one table; a gap whose lever has no currently-applicable action is dropped rather than shown as an inert row. The ranked list answers 'what's the single best thing to do next, across everything?'.

observed.title: Same-user device sync: three-way merge with first-class tombstones and a coordination-free deterministic tiebreak
observed.statement: When both endpoints belong to the same user, a true divergent conflict can be auto-resolved by last-writer-wins instead of queued for manual resolution — but two things are mandatory. (1) If entities hard-delete (no deleted_at column), deletions must sync as explicit tombstone entries, because otherwise a delete on one device is indistinguishable from 'never synced' and the row resurrects on the next pull. (2) The LWW ordering must be a total order both peers compute identically with no coordination: later modified_at wins, and an exact tie (including unparseable timestamps) breaks on a stable device-id comparison.

observed.title: Pair every calibration control with a live consequence sentence computed by the same predicate the automation uses
observed.statement: Threshold sliders and tuning levers should not end in a static caption. As the user drags, recompute the subject's status through the exact rule engine the automation will act on, and render a plain sentence stating what the system does at the current lines, right now ('X is past your red line — the system derives a goal to fix this now'). Scope the sentence to the triggers the control actually governs, and give the unmeasured case its own honest copy ('your lines take effect on the next measurement').
observed.detail_md:
Evidence: `src/features/teams/sub_factory/KpiConsole.tsx::ConsequencePreview`:

```tsx
/** D8 — calibration consequence preview. The threshold sliders used to end in a
 *  static "red derives a goal" caption; this turns the lever LEGIBLE by reading
 *  the live calibrated status (`kpiStatus`, which recomputes as the sliders move)
 *  and saying what the system does to THIS KPI at the current lines, right now.
 *  It scopes the statement to the thresholds the user is dragging (a breach is
 *  the slider's direct consequence); pace-lag is a separate trigger the slider
 *  doesn't control. */
```

The status comes from `src/features/teams/sub_kpis/kpiMath.ts::kpiTrack`, an exact port of the backend's `kpi_is_off_track` — so the preview can never disagree with what the derivation loop will actually fire on. This pattern makes any automation-driving threshold legible before it is saved.

observed.title: When an LLM refines an authored artifact, merge back only the prose and reject collapsed outputs — the result must never be worse than the base
observed.statement: An LLM 'specialization' pass over an authored artifact needs three structural guarantees: (1) only the prose fields (system prompt, instructions) are merged back — the deterministic structure (use cases, triggers, connectors) is never touched by the model; (2) every failure path (spawn error, unparseable output, nothing to merge) keeps the base and returns adjusted:false with a note, so the flow is never worse than the deterministic path; (3) a quality gate rejects a non-empty output whose prose collapsed to a fraction of the authored base (e.g. < 40% of a base > 200 chars) — truncation and models that gut the prompt are real, and 'shorter' must not silently replace 'authored'. Scale the model to divergence: defaults get a cheap wire-only pass, configured adoptions get a fuller model, escalated when the artifact carries high-stakes capabilities.

observed.title: Type a not-ready verdict by the remediation it needs, with a fail-closed 'misconfigured' sentinel
observed.statement: A readiness check that answers only ready/not-ready forces the UI to guess where to send the user. Return the setup KIND with the verdict — which remediation fixes it (add a credential, run the provider CLI's login, register a project, configure a vault) — and let the UI route accordingly, specializing generic hints with the concrete fix (the actual `vercel login` command, not 'run its login command'). Crucially, include a Misconfigured sentinel for declarations that are blank, corrupted, or reference a probe arm that was never wired: it is the fail-closed state that keeps a broken declaration from silently promoting the subject as ready.

observed.title: Order auth resolution portable-first: a stored credential always beats local CLI auth, which is only a fallback
observed.statement: When a capability can be satisfied either by a stored credential or by the vendor CLI's local login session, the stored credential must ALWAYS win when present — it is the only mode that survives leaving this machine (CI, another device, a headless run). The CLI probe is strictly a fallback for the no-credential case, because demanding a second hand-copied API token from users who already ran `vendor login` is friction they answer by skipping the integration entirely. Keep the probe off the hot path: memoise it in a TTL cache (long enough that one user action's many recomputes share a verdict, short enough that a fresh login is picked up) and bound every probe with a hard timeout since it runs on the UI's critical path.

observed.title: On Windows, probing a CLI through `cmd /C` hides the binary-absent signal — read the shell's own error text
observed.statement: npm-installed provider CLIs are `.cmd` shims on Windows; `CreateProcess` (and therefore `Command::new("vercel")`) cannot execute them, so probes must route through `cmd /C`. But `cmd` itself always spawns successfully, so the usual 'spawn error → binary absent' signal disappears: absence must be detected from the shell's stderr text ('is not recognized', 'command not found') or its 9009 exit code. Also pass CREATE_NO_WINDOW so no console flashes, close stdin so an interactive prompt fails fast instead of blocking, and treat a probe that hangs past its deadline as 'present but needs login' after killing it.

observed.title: A cancel path wired to a different registry than the spawn path is a silent no-op that keeps burning tokens
observed.statement: When start and cancel go through parallel process-tracking mechanisms (a single-slot domain API vs a multi-run map), a cancel that consults the map the spawner never populated does nothing: the cancellation flag stays false, the child keeps running (and billing), and the stale run later overwrites fresh state with its discarded result. Register and cancel MUST use the same registry API — and the cancel must additionally guard on the currently active run id so a stale id from the UI can't kill a newer run.

observed.title: Verify a freshly minted artifact with a real run and map the outcome three ways: proven, hard-block, or visibly unverified
observed.statement: After generating/adopting an artifact that claims to work (an agent, a pipeline, an integration), run one real verification of its first capability and refuse the binary pass/fail frame. Three-way mapping: value delivered → verified, status untouched; hard failure (precondition/failed) → downgrade the artifact's status so the run path blocks until fixed, AND raise a review; soft outcomes (no input available, unassessable, event-only) → leave it runnable but raise a visible review stating it was minted unverified. The one forbidden outcome is the old behaviour: silently presenting an unproven artifact as ready. Skip the run entirely when the artifact is already flagged (redundant cost), and make the gate fail-open — a verification that cannot be assessed must not brick a working artifact.

observed.title: Result rows and run rows speak different status vocabularies — predicate on evidence presence, not a status literal
observed.statement: When an eval pipeline stamps per-result verdicts (passed|failed|inconclusive) and per-run lifecycle states (generating|running|completed) into different tables, a WHERE status='completed' predicate on result rows matches nothing and silently empties every downstream rollup. Key 'is this a measurement' on the presence of at least one sub-score, and pin both the real verdict domain and the wrong literal in regression tests.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/db/src/repos/lab/ratings.rs` — the STATUS VOCABULARY doc-comment on `get_version_ratings` records the shipped bug (UAT 2026-07-20: 13 real results rendered as "Not measured" because `r.status = 'completed'` matched zero result rows; `completed` is a *run* status, `test_runner::verdict_status` only ever writes `passed|failed|inconclusive`). The fixed predicate counts a row as measured when `tool_accuracy_score OR output_quality_score OR protocol_compliance IS NOT NULL`. Three regression tests pin it: `arena_verdict_statuses_are_counted_as_measured` (all three verdicts count), `completed_is_not_a_result_status` (even a rogue `completed` row still counts because the predicate keys on score presence, not a status allowlist), and `scoreless_rows_are_not_counted`.

observed.title: When no worker survives a restart, fail every non-terminal run row at boot — an in-memory timeout cannot fix a persisted phantom
observed.statement: If run rows are driven by in-process tasks that die with the process, rows left non-terminal re-hydrate on every launch as phantom active runs (buttons disabled, cancel shown) and a frontend timeout only resets in-memory flags, so re-selection resurrects the phantom forever. Sweep all non-terminal rows to failed at startup with an explicit reason string; the sweep must be idempotent and must not touch terminal rows.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/db/src/repos/lab/mod.rs` `recover_interrupted_lab_runs` — flips `status NOT IN ('completed','failed','cancelled')` to `failed` with `error='Interrupted by app restart'` across all four `lab_*_runs` tables, because "No lab task survives a restart, so it is always safe to fail these at startup". The doc-comment records the live orphan `fd2c96c4` that wedged `isArenaRunning`. Tests: `recover_interrupted_lab_runs_reaps_only_orphans` (reaps a `running` arena row AND a `generating` eval row — proving the sweep is not keyed to one status string — while a completed row is untouched, and `get_all_active_progress` no longer surfaces the reaped rows) and `recover_interrupted_lab_runs_is_idempotent`. Differs from queue-recovery canon: these tasks are unrecoverable by design, so the right verb is fail-with-reason, not requeue.

observed.title: Stamp N parallel run/result table pairs from one declarative macro so every repo shares one CRUD and one status FSM
observed.statement: When a feature grows N structurally identical mode tables (run + result pair per mode), generate get/list/update-status/update-progress/delete for all of them from one declarative macro parameterized only by table names, types and result ordering. The shared update_run_status reads the current status and validates the transition against one FSM before writing, so a transition bug is fixed once for every mode.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/db/src/macros.rs:376` `macro_rules! lab_crud` is instantiated identically in `repos/lab/{arena,ab,eval,matrix,consensus}.rs` — each file declares only `run_table/result_table/types/result_order/mappers` and its mode-specific `create_*` functions. The generated `update_run_status` does `LabRunStatus::from_db(current).validate_transition(status)` before the COALESCE-preserving UPDATE, and maps `QueryReturnedNoRows` to a typed `NotFound` with the entity name baked in. Adding a sixth lab mode is one macro invocation plus its bespoke creators.

observed.title: A proposal queue against a moving target keeps exactly one pending row: filing a new one supersedes the old in the same transaction
observed.statement: When an automated cycle files promotion proposals against an incumbent that keeps moving, insert the new pending proposal and reject any older pending proposal for the same subject (status='rejected', decision_note='superseded by a newer cycle') inside one transaction, so the human review queue never accumulates stale head-to-heads. Resolution fails closed (UPDATE ... WHERE status='pending', 0 rows = error), and the row carries the incumbent's base_updated_at so the human-approved apply can CAS against a target that moved since filing.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/db/src/repos/lab/evolution_proposals.rs` — `create()` runs the supersede UPDATE + INSERT in one `tx`; module doc records "There is deliberately NO code path that resolves a proposal without a human command" and that apply lives elsewhere because it touches the live persona row transactionally (CAS on `base_updated_at` + change log). `resolve()` returns `Validation("not pending (missing or already decided)")` when rows==0 — no re-decisions, no downgrades. Tests: `newer_proposal_supersedes_pending_one` (and proves other subjects' pending rows are untouched), `create_files_pending_and_resolve_is_terminal`.

observed.title: A failed periodic cycle must still advance the retry-gate clock — but only successes may increment the counters
observed.statement: When a gate like 'at least N executions since last_cycle_at' throttles an expensive automated cycle, a persistently failing cycle that never stamps last_cycle_at re-fires on every trigger — a real money-burning retry storm with zero forward progress. Give the failure path its own bookkeeping call that advances only the cadence timestamp, while success-only stats (total_cycles, total_promotions) are bumped solely by the completion path.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/db/src/repos/lab/evolution.rs` `mark_cycle_attempted` — doc-comment: "Called on a *failed* terminal evolution path so `should_evolve` requires a fresh `min_executions_between` window before retrying. Without this ... the post-execution gate re-fires the same failing cycle on every subsequent execution — a real CLI/$$ retry storm ... `total_cycles` stays success-only (bumped solely by `complete_cycle`)." `complete_cycle` wraps its two UPDATEs (cycle terminal state + policy stats) in one transaction so the counters can never drift from the terminal row. Complements stamp-before-work canon: this is the stamp-on-failure half.

observed.title: Upsert on a nullable natural-key column via a UNIQUE expression index over COALESCE(col, '')
observed.statement: SQLite treats NULLs as distinct in UNIQUE constraints, so a natural key with an optional column silently duplicates. Build the unique index over the expression COALESCE(nullable_col, ''), write with ON CONFLICT(...) DO UPDATE that moves only the mutable fields (preserving the original id and created_at), and read back with the same COALESCE predicate.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/db/src/repos/lab/ratings.rs` `upsert_rating` — "Single-statement upsert backed by the UNIQUE expression index idx_lab_ratings_unique on (run_id, scenario_name, COALESCE(result_id, '')). On conflict we preserve the original id and created_at; only rating/feedback move." The read-back SELECT matches with `COALESCE(result_id,'') = COALESCE(?3,'')` so the caller gets the surviving row either way. Also guards the trust boundary first: rating outside 1..=5 is rejected with a typed Validation error before any SQL, so `Infinity`/`-5` junk never poisons aggregations.

observed.title: In an iterative agent loop, run only the required gates per iteration and batch informational gates into one final pass
observed.statement: Split verification gates into required (they gate area completion) and informational (they only decorate the report). Run required gates after every iteration, and run the informational set exactly once after the loop ends. Rerunning a slow build or advisory audit after each of ~70 iterations burns hours of wall-clock on results that change nothing.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/lib/harness/orchestrator.ts:179` — "Non-required gates (the 3-minute vite build, informational grep audits) don't affect area completion (only requiredFailures gates it below), yet the full suite used to rerun serially after every one of up to ~70 area iterations — hours of wall-clock on gates whose result only decorated the report. The full suite runs once after the loop instead." `verifier.ts` types the split (`VerificationGate.required`, `report.requiredFailures`), and the final pass at orchestrator.ts:310 runs `gates.filter(g => !g.required)` once, only when not paused.

observed.title: Give a long-running agent CLI loop a two-stage Ctrl-C: first pauses and persists, second force-quits
observed.statement: A single SIGINT on an autonomous loop should not discard hours of state. Handle the first interrupt by pausing the orchestrator (which persists plan/progress so a later run resumes), print that a second interrupt force-quits, and only exit hard on the second signal.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/lib/harness/run-harness.ts:179-188` — first SIGINT calls `orchestrator.pause()` (the loop checks `paused` between iterations and emits `harness:paused` — "state saved, safe to resume later", with `plan.json`/`progress.json` written after every iteration in `orchestrator.ts`), second SIGINT exits immediately. Pairs with the loop's resume path (`loadPlan()`/`loadProgress()` on start) so pause is genuinely cheap.

observed.title: In a measurement matrix, synthesize placeholder rows so unmeasured entities — especially the live config — stay visible and actionable
observed.statement: A version-by-model matrix built only from measured rows hides exactly the rows users must act on: the currently-live configuration that has no score yet, and versions never measured at all. Synthesize a placeholder row for the active (version, model) when it is unmeasured, and one null-model placeholder per otherwise-rowless version, then order active-first, measured-by-score, placeholders last.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/agents/sub_lab/libs/versionMatrixRows.ts` — `needsActivePlaceholder` synthesizes the active row "the user must always see (and be able to re-activate) the current config even before it has a score"; versions with no rating get a `key: `${version.id}::∅`` placeholder "so every version is visible and actionable"; within-version sort puts active first, then composite descending, unmeasured last. Placeholders carry `rating: null` / `composite: null` so downstream cells render 'not measured' rather than fabricated zeros.

observed.title: Stage a column-to-child-table migration as numbered ADR steps: dual-write best-effort while the old column stays canonical
observed.statement: To move data from a JSON column into a normalized child table without a risky cutover, dual-write during a transition phase in which the old column remains the canonical read source: child-table insert failures are logged and swallowed (analytics underreport, user data never corrupts), inserts are INSERT OR IGNORE for replay-safety, and each repo's create path calls one shared write helper. The ADR numbers the steps so 'drop the JSON columns' is an explicit later step, not an ambient hope.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/db/src/repos/lab/mod.rs` `write_tool_calls_child_rows` — "Failures are logged and swallowed during this transition phase: the JSON column remains the canonical source until the cutover step (step 6), so a partial child-table write does not corrupt user data ... ADR: 2026-05-02-lab-tool-calls-child-table." All five `create_result` sites (`arena.rs`, `ab.rs`, `eval.rs`, `matrix.rs`, `consensus.rs`) carry the matching comment "The parent-table JSON columns are dropped in step 7 of this ADR", and the reader (`ScenarioDetailPanel.tsx:124`) tolerates legacy rows. The claim here is the staged-cutover choreography (canonicality + best-effort + numbered steps), not the child-table modeling itself.

observed.title: After promoting a new default, enumerate the per-item overrides that now diverge and offer clear-or-keep — keep is a first-class no-op
observed.statement: Promoting a new default (model, template, policy) leaves per-item override pins untouched, so items silently keep executing on the old value. Immediately after a successful promotion, surface a reconciliation dialog listing exactly which items still pin something else, let the user clear each pin (write through the same shared mutator as every other edit — no parallel write path) or keep it, and skip reconciliation entirely when the promotion write itself failed.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/agents/sub_lab/components/versions_table/PostActivationReconcileDialog.tsx` — "per-use-case `model_override` pins are left untouched, so a use case can silently keep executing on the old model ... Clearing writes through the shared design-context mutator (no parallel write path); dismissing changes nothing — 'keep pin' is a first-class, no-op choice." The launcher (`LabVersionsTable.tsx:136-160`) guards `if (!ok) return; // Activation failed ... nothing to reconcile`, and per-row cleared state only flips after `res.applied` confirms the write.

observed.title: Resolve a config cascade once into per-field {value, source, isOverridden} provenance and render inheritance from that shape
observed.statement: When effective configuration merges agent > workspace > global > default layers, do the resolution once (server-side) into a shape where every field carries its value plus which layer supplied it and whether it overrides the inherited one. The UI then renders per-row inheritance badges and inherited-vs-overridden counts from data instead of re-deriving precedence, and secret-typed fields are masked in the provenance view — including suppressing the hover tooltip that would otherwise leak the raw value.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/agents/sub_model_config/components/EffectiveConfigPanel.tsx:64-69` consumes `EffectiveModelConfig` fields of shape `{value, source, isOverridden}`; `ConfigInheritanceBadge.tsx:5-17` maps each `ConfigSource` to icon+color+tooltip from one table; `EffectiveConfigPanel.tsx:21-36,108` gates both the rendered value and the `title` attribute on the `mask` prop (`field.value != null && !mask ? String(field.value) : undefined`). Fetch side: `hooks/useEffectiveConfig.ts` re-resolves per persona/refreshKey with a cancelled-flag guard.

observed.title: A hardcoded $0 from an unmetered provider is 'cost unknown', not 'free' — flag it at aggregation and render 'not tracked'
observed.statement: Local/self-hosted providers whose runner hardcodes per-call cost to 0.0 will win every cost ranking and read as free. Stamp a cost_unknown flag on the aggregate wherever the provider is known to not report cost, exclude flagged rows from value verdicts, and render 'not tracked' instead of $0.000.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: backend — `src-tauri/db/src/repos/lab/ratings.rs`: "Ollama's per-call cost is hardcoded 0.0 in the runner — a zero here is 'unknown', not 'free'. Flag it so the value verdict skips it" (`cost_unknown: provider == OLLAMA` on `LabVersionRating`). Frontend — `LabVersionsTable.tsx:233-237`: "surface 'not tracked' rather than a misleading $0.000 that reads as 'free'"; `reportGenerator.ts` `fmtRowCost` renders `'not tracked'` when `costUnknown` so exported client reports carry the same honesty.

observed.title: A parser cache of size one shared by sibling consumers thrashes on every render — bound the LRU above the visible working set
observed.statement: Caching an expensive pure parse behind an LRU that holds exactly one entry breaks the moment two sibling components parse different inputs in the same frame: each evicts the other's entry, reference stability dies, and Object.is-based store selectors re-fire forever. Key the cache by the raw input string, size it to comfortably exceed the number of simultaneously-visible consumers, and share one frozen empty result so the miss path is also referentially stable.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/agents/sub_lab/use-cases/UseCasesList.tsx:23-73` — the comment records that the previous LRU-1 cache "held exactly one entry, so any sibling component parsing a different persona's string would immediately evict it and break reference stability", defeating zustand `Object.is` selectors; the fix is a bounded string-keyed LRU plus one frozen shared empty object. Related idiom in the same pocket: `ArenaHistory.tsx:16-17` hoists a module-level `EMPTY` constant instead of `?? []` in memo deps ("a fresh [] each render would change the identity of every downstream useMemo dep").

observed.title: Put an explicit cell budget on quadratic diff work and degrade through a ladder of coarser algorithms
observed.statement: An O(n*m) DP diff on user-sized inputs must check its cell count before allocating anything. Strip the common prefix/suffix first (which alone often brings the middle under budget), re-check the budget on the remainder, then fall through a graded ladder: word-level LCS, line-level LCS, and finally a whole-replaced (all-removed + all-added) rendering. Every rung still produces a correct, just coarser, result.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/agents/sub_lab/shared/labPrimitives.ts:25,91-147` — `MAX_DP_CELLS = 250_000` with a cheap upper-bound check before any allocation; the fallback ladder is prefix/suffix strip → re-check middle → word-LCS → line-LCS → all-removed+all-added. The budget constant is named and central, so the tradeoff is tunable in one place.

observed.title: An optional prop that is the sole conduit of a feedback loop can silently sever it — wire it at every call site and say it is load-bearing
observed.statement: When human feedback flows to a learning/improvement engine only through one UI prop, shipping a call site without that prop closes the entire loop with zero errors: the feature keeps rendering, the table that feeds the improver just never gets rows. Audit that every renderer of the feedback control passes the persistence props, and leave a comment at the call site naming the downstream consumer so the next refactor cannot drop it unknowingly.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/agents/sub_lab/components/arena/ArenaHistory.tsx:115-121` — "`lab_user_ratings` is the ONLY source of `user_feedback` for `generate_targeted_improvements` — so leaving these props off this call site (as shipped) closed the sole path for a person to tell the improvement engine which output was actually wrong (UAT 2026-07-20). Keep them wired." Companion finding in the same audit: the `lab_improve_prompt` binding had zero callers while the button seeded only ~4 scalars (`ImprovePromptButton.tsx:55-68`), i.e. rich judge diagnosis was being downgraded before reaching the improver.

observed.title: When the owning entity switches mid-run, clear the stale run id AND best-effort cancel the orphaned backend run
observed.statement: Switching the selected entity while an expensive comparison run is in flight must do two things: reset the local run state so the new entity's UI can never render the old entity's output (a cross-workspace prompt leak), and fire a best-effort cancel at the backend run so the orphan stops burning budget. A run id obtained after an await is only adopted if the entity token captured before the await is still current — otherwise it is cancelled immediately.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/agents/sub_model_config/components/compare/ModelABCompare.tsx:53-96` — `capturePersonaToken` before `startArena`, then `if (!token.isStillCurrent()) { void cancelArena(runId); return; }` ("Persona may have changed during the await. Don't adopt the runId into a different persona's UI"); the entity-switch effect does `setActiveRunId(prevId => { if (prevId) void cancelArena(prevId); return null; })` with a comment naming both the leak ("potentially leak sensitive prompts across workspaces") and the spend. Extends the snapshot-id-before-await canon with the server-side cancel half.

observed.title: A one-shot auto-load latched on 'still empty' re-fires forever when empty is the legitimate answer — latch on attempted instead
observed.statement: Auto-triggering an initial fetch 'while the surface is empty' loops when the fetch legitimately returns nothing: the condition stays true after completion, so the effect reschedules the refresh on every idle tick. Latch the trigger on an attempted ref (or last-attempt timestamp), not on the emptiness condition, so one genuine empty answer ends the retry.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/overview/sub_leaderboard/components/LeaderboardPage.tsx:20-36` — "an empty fleet ... still ends with isEmpty true after the refresh completes, so without the attempted-guard this effect re-scheduled refresh() every ~200ms-2s"; fixed with an attempted ref around the `requestIdleCallback` (with `setTimeout` fallback) initial load.

observed.title: Label a non-differentiating metric as tied or unavailable instead of letting it masquerade as ranking signal
observed.statement: When a displayed metric currently cannot differentiate subjects — every row shares one fleet-wide value, or there is no honest prior period for a trend — say so inline (a 'tied' chip with the known limitation, no trend arrow) rather than rendering a column or arrow that looks like signal. Detect the degenerate case from the data itself (a Set of the values has size 1) so the label disappears the day the metric becomes real.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/overview/sub_leaderboard/components/LeaderboardMatrixView.tsx:118-122,160-165` — `speedAllEqual` computed from a `Set` of values renders a "tied" chip: "Identical for every agent — latency is mapped fleet-wide, not per-agent (known bug)". Same honesty rule for trends in `DashboardHomeMissionControl.tsx:573-587`: "When compare is off there is no honest prior period, so the tile shows no arrow rather than the old front-half/back-half heuristic that lied over a single window."

observed.title: A filter wired only into the primary backend query silently no-ops on views fed from a different source — apply the facet at every source
observed.statement: When one surface renders data from two sources (a filtered backend query for the main view, a precomputed summary for a secondary view), filter controls wired only into the query become dead controls on the secondary view: the dropdown and clickable tiles render, do nothing, and raise no error. Apply the active facet client-side to every source the surface renders, and sort before filtering so filtering preserves the established order.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/overview/sub_knowledge/components/KnowledgeGraphDashboard.tsx:103-121` — "the no-persona view renders summary.top_patterns (which the query never touches) — without this the type dropdown and the clickable KPI tiles silently no-op there", plus "Sort before filtering — filtering preserves order".

observed.title: Clamp the gauge, print the true number when a metric can legitimately exceed its nominal scale
observed.statement: Some scored dimensions legitimately exceed 100 (bonus completions, over-achievement). Clamp only the visual bar width to the scale so layout never breaks, but render the real value as the label — silently capping the number hides the over-achievement, and letting the bar overflow breaks the chart.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/overview/sub_certification/components/DimensionBars.tsx:13-15` — "Bars can exceed 100 (e.g. cascade_completion=120 when extra roles fire); clamp the visual width but show the true number."

observed.title: Honor reduced-motion with a real render branch to plain DOM, not by zeroing animation durations
observed.statement: Zeroed durations still mount the animation library's wrappers, still schedule its effects, and can still flash. When prefers-reduced-motion is set, branch to a plain element tree that never imports motion wrappers for that render, and also skip derived motion props like per-row animationDelay so stagger math cannot reintroduce movement.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/agents/sub_lab/components/shared/LabStaggerGroup.tsx:31-35,60-62` — `if (!shouldAnimate) return <div ...>` on both container and item, framer-motion skipped entirely. Same discipline in `sub_director/components/PersonaCoachingTable.tsx:138-144` (reduced-motion skips both the animation class and the per-row `animationDelay`) and explicit-intent handling in `DashboardHomeMissionControl.tsx:665-668`.

observed.title: In an N-way comparison, an expected participant with zero result rows is a failure signal, not an empty state
observed.statement: Type the aggregation of a comparison cell as a three-way result — ok(metrics), missing(participantId), empty — where 'missing' means the caller asked for this participant but no rows carry its id (its run failed or never dispatched) and 'empty' means no run has produced anything yet. The UI then renders 'X produced no results — run may have failed' for missing instead of a generic no-data placeholder that hides the failure.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/agents/sub_model_config/libs/compareHelpers.ts:62-88` — `AggregateResult = {status:'ok'} | {status:'missing', modelId} | {status:'empty'}` with the doc-comment "Callers should distinguish 'missing' from 'empty' so the UI can surface 'Model X produced no results — run may have failed' instead of a generic 'no data' message"; consumed by the red banner in `ModelABCompare.tsx:167-174`.
